+ Lifestyle Medicine Digital Nudging SLR (`cognitive-science-and-ux/lifestyle-medicine-digital-nudging-slr/`) — Applies Taniar, King, Manger & Carlisle (Front. Digit. Health 8:1799205, 2026; PRISMA-ScR, 52 studies across six databases): the first scoping review mapping digital nudging across ALL lifestyle-medicine pillars — four inductively-derived categories (one-way nudging 23 studies; system-interaction nudging 14; peer-interaction 4; self-nudging 11) within a passive/active conceptual frame, with technologies as delivery platforms not categories. Findings: nutrition + physical activity >75% of studies; sleep has one study and the connection pillar ZERO; choice architecture (ordering, defaults, Nutri-score labelling) is the consistently effective one-way form, warnings risk habituation, emerging-technology nudges face the novelty cliff; ~⅓ of studies still evaluate usability rather than behavior change; the named frontier is AI personalization over comprehensive user profiles. + Stripe-OpenRouter Inference Acquisition (`monetization-and-revenue/stripe-openrouter-inference-acquisition/`) — Analyzes Stripe's acquisition of OpenRouter (agreed AND completed Aug 20 2026; reported ~$7.5B — Stripe's largest-ever; ~$1.5B founders / ~$6B investors per NYT; ~53.6× its ~$140M July annualized revenue; $1.3B valuation in May 2026): a payments company buying the layer that chooses an AI supplier for each request. The analytical core: **each route has become a purchase order** (buyer, supplier, quantity, price) — the request replaced the vendor as the unit of model choice; agents put allocation on the critical path (budget enforcement, fallbacks, capacity reactions mid-work); the order book sees demand before vendors do (Ox Alpha, the free anonymous model that topped OpenRouter usage before Z.ai identified it as GLM-5.3-Flash — distribution + zero price supplied what branding usually does; observation becomes distribution); policy lives in the route (Palo Alto's reported $120–140M Portkey acquisition brackets the security layer at ~$130M vs $7.5B for the transaction volume). The price assumes plurality survives: if inference costs halve into pricing or one provider wins cost+quality+capacity, routing loses dispersion to exploit — at 53.6× Stripe has little room. Sibling framing with NVIDIA-HF (`open-commons-acquisition-neutrality-2026`): own the layer everyone passes through; both re-centralize what open weights decentralized; portable multi-provider architectures are the escape hatch. Pairs with open-commons-acquisition-neutrality-2026, openrouter-inference-routing-economics, agent-runtime-model-pricing-disaggregation, ai-infra-consolidation-acquisition-lens-2026. **2026-09-06 (cycle 20, run 1):** x402 Free-Riding Attack Surface (`ai-agents-and-workflows/x402-free-riding-attack-surface/`) — Applies the first systematic security analysis of x402 (Ling, Huang, Du, Chen, Zhou, Wu & Wang, arXiv:2605.30998, May 29/June 22 2026; vendor pre-disclosure; minia2a plain-English map Sept 3): five formal invariants (payment integrity, value consistency, context binding, authorization uniqueness, execution conservation) violated by FOUR reproducible flaw classes — F1 cross-resource substitution (signed authorization not bound to the resource; 100/100 reproductions; TS/Python omit the check, Java trusts mutable JSON, Go trusts the facilitator; fix = EIP-712 context binding over H(Method∥URI∥Body)), F2 duplicate-settlement race (verify-settle decoupling window; 6% duplicate delivery; fix = stateful nonce linearization), F3 allowance overdraft (upto-scheme TOCTOU; 97.76% leakage, ~100% long-context variant; fix = reserve-commit two-phase locking), F4 denial of settlement (ingress/settlement rate asymmetry; 86.95–100% leakage; fix = failure-closed design — "reliability issues should result in denial of service, not denial of payment"). THREE OF FOUR ARE MERCHANT-SIDE — a seller can silently subsidize free riders at up to 100%. Defense triple (G1 crypto rate limiting, G2 adaptive hidden-compute billing −47%, G3 bounded-loss streaming ~$0.00047/interruption): zero attacks in 500 adversarial trials at 2.8% overhead; proven structural limit — no output-only pay-per-token pricing can be both fair and bounded (√(1+Θ) manipulation gap). Four-question audit: context-bound? nonce-once? funds-locked-before-execution? fail-closed settlement? Pairs with x402-production-checklist (add the audit), agent-settlement-protocol-asp-2026 (the commerce tier above), agentic-trust-security-protocols-2026. Why V1 hit a wall: per-request on-chain settlement fails high-frequency APIs, multi-call agent workflows, market platforms, and multi-chain. The competitor framing: x402's real adversary is the old internet architecture that separates payments from web requests — "Web3 asked how money goes on-chain; x402 asks how money enters HTTP." Privacy flag: wallet-as-identity is pseudonymous but session reuse eases behavioral linkage — session-scoped identity segregation is a design requirement. Pairs with mcp-enterprise-adoption-2026 (refreshed with this addendum), agentic-ai-zero-trust-compliance, onboarding-acceleration-protocol, agent-reputation-identity-framework. + Social-Learning Ecology Diffusion (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/social-learning-ecology-diffusion/`) — Applies Veltri & Acerbi (Behavioural Public Policy, Sept 2, 2026, open access; ABM: 400 agents, 150 steps, 100 paired replications, code on OSF): an identical seeding campaign (5% control vs 25% treatment) meets FOUR fates depending on the population's social-learning strategy — CONFORMIST majorities stall it (25% sits below the threshold; both arms collapse to zero), prestige-biased learners drift it (gap persists IF prestige tracks who benefits), PAYOFF-BIASED learners cascade it (in both arms — saturating the system), random copiers preserve the largest residual advantage (78% vs 69%). KEY FINDINGS: conformist-dominant mixtures still stall even with a 30% minority of other learners followed 10× longer; payoff-driven success erases its own evidence (endpoint measurement reports a null — the intervention changed diffusion TIMING, not reach — a mechanism for why scaled intervention effects underperform trials); final lift peaks at ~20% payoff-biased share. Design rules: diagnose the learning ecology before choosing the seed (threshold-targeting for conformists; credible community demonstrators for prestige; visible attributable outcomes + matched time-since-seeding measurement for payoff; broad seeding for weak structure). Ethics: amplifying prestige/payoff cues decides whose status gets amplified. Four citation-discipline rules: modality caveat always; use the domain split to position claims; pair neuroforecasting with small-N reality; treat region-naming as canonical pattern not law. Pairs with neurophysiological-consumer-meta-analysis (the effect-size ceiling), predictive-neuromarketing-bayesian-framework, consumer-mentalizing-eeg-social-cognition. + Consumer Neurophysiological Moderators 2026 (`marketing-and-content/consumer-neurophysiological-moderators-2026/`) — Applies Nagpal, Bala, Singh, Yadav & Paliwal (Frontiers in Psychology, Mar 18, 2026; N=609 Delhi–NCR digitally active consumers, PLS-SEM, S–O–R × dual-process): the structural test of six neuromarketing determinants on impulsivity via perceived efficacy — EMOTIONAL APPEALS strongest (β=0.469), COGNITIVE PROCESSING second (β=0.378 — System 2 credibility cues AMPLIFY impulse response, the headline nuance), sensory triggers (β=0.173) and neuro-pricing (β=0.134) significant; SCARCITY/URGENCY (p=.095) and ENDORSEMENT INFLUENCE (p=.127) FAILED — saturation hypothesis: repetitive time-bound promotions and influencer cues have faded through reduced perceived authenticity. Traits both direct (β=0.416) and moderating (β=0.075): the efficacy-impulsivity link strengthens with dispositional susceptibility — trait-informed segmentation is mandatory. Rules: lead with emotional narrative, substantiate with structure; deprioritize countdown timers; treat endorsements as table stakes; segment by susceptibility; keep pricing transparent. Three firm vignettes: Liberty insurance (EEG/GSR/facial-coding chatbot optimization — "quote in 5 minutes" pre-launch targets), TUI (facial-coding destination matching prototype), Zyro (pre-trained saliency AI heatmaps — the privacy-minimal attention pattern). The framework's own five ethical guardrails: informed consent, transparency, data minimization, consumer choice (opt-out WITHOUT losing essential service — the test), algorithmic accountability. Rules: treat neuro signals as a distinct class needing consent surfaces clickstreams never required; map inference → named touchpoint action; prefer pretrained saliency for attention questions; keep the firm journey auditable. SKILL.md. + Agent Settlement Protocol ASP 2026 (`ai-agents-and-workflows/agent-settlement-protocol-asp-2026/` — SKILL.md + references/formal-analysis-agent-payments-evidence.md) — Applies the Agentic Settlement Protocol (Mohammadkhani, Khekade & Kakkad, XDC AI, arXiv:2609.02208, draft v0.6 Aug 31/Sept 2 2026): the first specification for refundable, delayed-fulfilment agent commerce on stablecoin rails — the missing layer above x402, whose atomic one-shot payments "suit metered access and fail commerce" (a plumber visit, a physical order, a flight, a freelance deliverable is large, cancellable, and must not become the seller's money until delivery). THE CORE DIAGNOSIS: every online business runs a fulfilment engine (order-management stock timeouts, scheduling slot expiry, invoice due dates, travel ticketing limits) with its own clock — escrow and engine are two uncoordinated distributed systems, and no payment-layer spec (x402/CPP/AP2/ACP) addresses the coupling. THE FIVE CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) three-deadline hold model H1–H4 (issuance deadline + escrow expiry + engine inventory expiry with submission-inclusion-finality margin; Proposition 1 — no inventory ever issued against reclaimable funds; H3 enforced on-chain by the vault, not operator discipline); (2) fulfilment-verification ladder D/C/A/S (rung = part of the signed Offer so the buyer agent knows the trust position before signing; rung C explicitly an auditable data-commitment model, not cryptographic fulfilment); (3) engine-authoritative refunds + bounded operator exposure (rolling reserve, settlement delay, exposure caps, ATOMIC exposure reservation at Offer issuance — without it a $90k-of-$100k seller takes 100 concurrent $1k quotes to $190k liability; Proposition 3 caps simultaneous-default loss at λ·pool); (4) self-dealing-proof revenue share (Proposition 2 — net loss f·amount·(1−s) per self-referred charge); (5) single-currency invariant + normative interfaces (x402 asp scheme, vault ABI, operator/connector APIs with the never-retry-a-timed-out-commit rule, ASP-Lite/Core/Full conformance + 17-case executable suite). Deployment: ERC-4337 buyer accounts with on-chain spend caps (compromised-agent blast radius bounded), reclaim never pausable, platform-connector onboarding in days. Honest caveats: design paper, no deployed measurements (fault-injection plan specified, results to follow); vendor-affiliated authors. Paired with the SAME-WEEK formal-methods track: Jiang et al., "A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols" (arXiv:2609.00060, Aug 30 2026) — Tamarin formalization of x402/MPP/ACP/AP2 exposing 46 known + 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency findings across 86 verification cases, consolidated into 18 shared security principles; central claim: delegated authorization must remain consistent with its economic and service effects across actors, states, and protocol stages. Together they mark the moment agent payments attract formal-methods scrutiny — the maturation curve payments and consensus went through. Pairs with x402-production-checklist (the metered-layer complement), mcp-payment-support-specification, agentic-commerce-trust-design, erc8004-empirical-trust-reality-check-2026 (cited by ASP's authors), transaction-closure-delegated-ai-governance. A-Tech alignment: open source (normative public spec + executable conformance suite), privacy (on-chain spend-cap blast-radius bounding; charge-metadata privacy flagged as open gap), financial freedom (bounded-exposure design makes the seller side viable for small businesses; days-not-months connector onboarding), practical (two-clocks diagnosis + rung ladder + buyer-agent checklist; "x402 pays for tokens — ASP pays for the plumber"). SKILL.md + references/sovereign-tech-standards-evidence-base.md. + Socratic-vs-Unrestricted Brain Sensing 2026 (`cognitive-science-and-ux/socratic-vs-unrestricted-brain-sensing-2026/`) — Applies the MIT Media Lab study "Socrates went Nuclear" (Clin Deffarges, Kosmyna & Maes, HAI'26, arXiv:2609.00584, Sept 1 2026; N=50, Muse consumer EEG, zero-prior-knowledge domain: nuclear safety protocols): the first brain-sensing comparison of three AI interaction strategies for learning — unrestricted ChatGPT-style bot vs Socratic hints-only bot vs non-conversational EEG-adaptive tutor (difficulty adjusted in real time from cognitive engagement, engagement measured in ALL conditions). THE MEASURED PARADOX: the unrestricted chatbot produced the LARGEST learning gains (Δ, p<.03, d>0.80 vs both constrained modes) while the adaptive condition produced the HIGHEST EEG engagement (p=.018) — and cluster analysis of usage shows the unrestricted group mostly adopted direct answer-retrieval while the Socratic group initially reasoned through hints then PROGRESSIVELY DISENGAGED. The authors' reading: unrestricted AI's success "is not an evidence of deeper learning, but rather a result of the immediate post-test evaluation after the training phase." SIX DESIGN RULES: match the evaluation horizon to the claim (immediate post-test = retrieval, not learning — long-term retention is the missing measurement in essentially all AI-education studies); constrained designs must earn continued engagement, not just compliance (monotony, not Socratic method, is the failure mode); engagement ≠ gains and gains ≠ learning; instrument engagement to make the tradeoff visible (consumer EEG sufficed; proxies for products: response latency, reformulation rate, hint-follow-through, struggle-time); answer-retrieval is the default gravity (deeper processing must be designed in, not merely not blocked); ship adaptive-with-guardrails, not guardrails-alone. Policy translation: neither extreme survives the evidence — unrestricted maximizes short-term scores through retrieval, pure Socratic constraints disengage, adaptive engagement-targeting is the defensible middle. Honest caveats: single domain, N=50, immediate post-test only, Muse-class EEG, exploratory clustering. Pairs with ai-brain-fry-defense, cognitive-surrender-defense, ai-character-fnirs-eye-tracking-design, micro-learning-just-in-time-ai, neuroadaptive-attention-engineering. A-Tech alignment: open source (consumer-EEG replicable measurement pattern), privacy (biometric-adjacent engagement sensing — on-device + aggregate-only consent posture flagged as mandatory), financial freedom (adaptive+constrained hybrid implementable with open-weight models and cheap proxies, not enterprise BCI), practical (6 design rules + the evaluation-horizon rule). SKILL.md. + RecalibrateGPT AI-Fatigue Operators 2026 (`cognitive-science-and-ux/recalibrategpt-ai-fatigue-operators-2026/`) — Applies RecalibrateGPT (Wani, UIST Adjunct 2026, arXiv:2609.00506, Sept 1 2026; two pilot studies, N=12 advanced LLM users): the first interaction-level framework for conversational AI fatigue — the type→read→retype loop that produces cognitive load and task abandonment. THE CORE REFRAME: AI fatigue "is not just a model-quality issue but an interaction-flow cost that interfaces can remove" — some "the model isn't good enough" complaints are actually "the transcript is a hostile workspace" complaints, fixable in the UI. FOUR-TYPE FATIGUE TAXONOMY: retyping (re-describing established context), scanning (hunting long transcripts for earlier outputs), decision paralysis (too many open response options), context drift (frame quietly moved; mental model and transcript diverge). FIVE CROSS-TURN OPERATORS, each targeting a distinct fatigue type and acting on the full history in one click via an AssistiveButton (three palette layouts: Vertical/Arc/Tablet): ANCHOR (pin the persistent frame → drift/retyping), REPLAY (resurface an earlier output → scanning), DELTA (explicit diff from a prior version → scanning/paralysis), SCOPE (bound the next response → paralysis), STEER (redirect mid-generation without restarting → drift/retyping). Pilot evidence: perceived workload HALVED (NASA-TLX=2.7) at high usability (SUS=86.5) — directional only (N=12, self-report, no longitudinal data; the contribution is the framework, not a validated instrument). Includes the 5-question conversational-surface design checklist and its position in the library's fatigue/load stack (measurement and review-workflow sides already held; this adds the interaction-operator layer for chat surfaces specifically). (`monetization-and-revenue/openai-cursor-severance-case-2026/`) — Applies OpenAI's formal termination of frontier-model supply to Cursor (change-of-control provision triggered by SpaceX's $60B acquisition of Anysphere; cutoff date November 12 2026; Cursor barred from the upcoming Astra architecture; TechTalks/Ben Dickson, Sept 4 2026) as the pattern skill for closed-API dependency-severing — the third case after Anthropic's <5-days-notice severing of Windsurf (June 2025, triggered by OpenAI's reported ~$3B acquisition talks; Jared Kaplan: "odd for us to be selling Claude to OpenAI"). THE STRUCTURAL READING: closed frontier labs no longer behave as neutral digital utilities — they act as competitors of their best customers whenever the customer becomes an acquisition target; corporate politics, not service quality, decides whether a product keeps working. THE FOUR BYOK BREAKDOWN MODES: (1) feature collapse — pooled-infrastructure features stop entirely (Cursor Tab autocompletion, auto-routing, background cloud agents, CLI tooling); (2) billing shock — $20/mo pooled subscription → raw per-token API billing (agentic loops can run dozens-to-hundreds of dollars in days); (3) compliance break — Cursor's native enterprise zero-data-retention guarantee does NOT apply to custom keys (an immediate enterprise procurement blocker); (4) rate-limit wall — organizational TPM throttling that pooled piping bypassed. WHY CURSOR SURVIVED: exposure engineered to ~5% of user traffic before the cutoff — two-pool billing (proprietary Composer 2.5 + Grok at double quotas/$0.50-M; third-party frontier under tight caps), the highest-volume feature (Cursor Tab) running entirely on custom-trained low-latency models without OpenAI endpoints, Auto Router deflecting routine work (30-60% inference-cost cuts), and SpaceX Colossus compute backing — closed frontier labs now treated as disposable scratchpads for exploration, production anchored to first-party models + open weights + multi-provider failover. OpenAI's counter-cost: blinding itself to one of the richest coding-telemetry datasets (accept/reject/modify signals feed RL); Anthropic reaffirmed staying on Cursor. DECISION FRAMEWORK: run the 5%-test (what share of core product FUNCTION survives a termination notice tomorrow); anchor production to open weights + private fine-tuning + failover routing (closed APIs for exploration and the hard-reasoning slice only); treat telemetry as a strategic asset (whoever hosts the primary coding loop owns the improvement signal); extend dependency review to routers (Stripe-OpenRouter and NVIDIA-HF absorbed both neutral intermediaries in the same three weeks); survival asymmetry — an independent company loses ~5% of traffic in a cutoff, a dependent one loses 100% of native features. Pairs with open-commons-acquisition-neutrality-2026 (the consolidation counterpart), openrouter-inference-routing-economics (the router acquired in the same window), give-away-keep-matrix-oss-ai (open-weights-as-strategy, empirically validated), ai-inference-investment-rotation-2026, agentic-coder-segmentation-2026. A-Tech alignment: open source (model independence as survival trait, not ideology), privacy (the ZDR break shows the privacy surface lives in the pooled-integration layer), financial freedom (owned/open weights = owning the meter; dependence = rent subject to political repricing), practical (four-BYOK-breakdown table + 5%-test for vendor-risk reviews; content angle "Your AI product has a landlord — and landlords evict"). SKILL.md. + AI Assistance Distributional Inversion (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/ai-assistance-distributional-inversion/`) — Applies Holz, Perez-Truglia, Simon & Zentner ("Taxpayer Behavior in the Age of AI: A Field Experiment on Property Tax Appeals," NBER WP 35632, Aug 2026; preregistered AEARCTR-0018430; Dallas County TX; 645 households; Claude-powered chatbot on an appeal-assistance website with TaxBot vs Marina persona secondary randomization): the first field-RCT INVERSION of the AI-productivity literature. Chatbot access raised direct appeal filing 9.1pp (41.4%→50.5%, p=0.021; adjusted 10.5pp p=0.006; event-study falsification clean 2021-2025) with 78% take-up and no crowd-out of human agents (-0.2pp ns); benchmarked as a ~$425 expected-savings equivalent and nearly 2× a mailed step-by-step guide + tailored argument (4.98pp, Nathan et al. 2025) — on top of a control site already carrying substantial assistance. Mechanism: households used the chatbot to EXERCISE JUDGMENT (91.5% asked whether to file; 50.8% which comparables support the case; 44.6% what opinion-of-value; bot recommended filing with rationale in 98.1% of conversations) and reshaped feature use (evidence-document creation 7%→18.4%; comparable-report downloads 76%→54%). THE INVERSION: effects were SMALLER for less-advantaged households (BA+ +25.0pp vs no-BA +5.8pp, p=0.069; higher-value +13.5pp vs +5.5pp; non-minority +14.8pp vs +7.2pp — imprecise but consistent across all three splits) while TAKE-UP gaps were much smaller than OUTCOME gaps — the divergence arises after take-up, in how effectively households translate guidance into action; universal access to conversational judgment-support may WIDEN existing disparities. Design rules: audit the outcome distribution, not just the average (pre-register subgroup analysis on the dimension the service claims to equalize); measure take-up AND conversion-to-action separately (a take-up-flat/downstream-flat subgroup = usage-quality problem needing structured guidance, not outreach); pair universal AI access with scaffolding for the least-advantaged slice; expect the inversion in judgment-heavy consequence-heavy domains (tax, legal, benefits, investing) — the productivity-literature pattern does not automatically transfer. Caveats: working paper, single county, sample overrepresents appeal-prone households, subgroup effects imprecisely estimated (education split only marginally significant). Pairs with agentic-coding-returns-to-expertise (the moderation literature this inverts), kiyosaki-ai-wealth-transfer (the equity caveat), belief-profile-targeting-rct (friction diagnosis), digital-addiction-economics-2026. A-Tech alignment: financial freedom (the equity caveat for AI-for-wealth content), practical (take-up vs outcome-gap audit table), open source (replicable preregistered design), privacy (transcript sensitivity flagged). SKILL.md. + Cost-Salience Variety Margin (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/cost-salience-variety-margin/`) — Applies Hong, Riyanto, Yan & Huo ("Making organization's cost salient: A natural field experiment," JEBO vol. 248, 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.jebo.2026.107634; university staff ordering stationery online at university cost; cost visibility randomized in the ordering interface): the margin rule for third-party-cost salience — displaying the organization's cost did NOT change ordering frequency or quantity (intensive margin) but DID cut item VARIETY (extensive margin), producing a 27% overall consumption reduction; individuals partially internalize the external effects of their actions when the organization's cost is salient. THE PLACEMENT RULE: surface third-party cost at the ADD-ITEM step (new service, new region, new model tier, new add-on) not at checkout or invoice — the invoice arrives too late; the add-item decision is where cloud/SaaS/token sprawl happens; expect no effect on core usage volume (don't fight it — pair salience-for-sprawl with rightsizing-for-volume); for AI spend specifically this adds the institutional framing to the library's individual-metering skills ("this subagent fan-out just cost the team $0.40" at request time targets variety, not guilt over necessary volume). Ethical note: the effect runs through internalized external cost — a boost-style information intervention, distinct from shame displays that risk reactance/gaming. Caveats: single org, stationery domain, one-shot; variety effects may partially reflect one-time rationalization; cloud/SaaS generalization is mechanism-parallel analogy. Pairs with ai-agent-finfops-cost-optimization, plan-limit-cognitive-thirst-trap (individual metering vs this org-level lever), nudge-complementarity-benefit-cost, digital-addiction-economics-2026. **2026-09-04 (cycle 18, run 2):** Stem-Cell Donation Dropout Nudge (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/stem-cell-donation-dropout-nudge/`) — Applies Kato, Ohtake, Kurosawa, Yoshiuchi & Fukuda ("Exploring information provision to promote stem cell donation: Evidence from a field experiment of the Japan Marrow Donor Program," Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization vol. 248, 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.jebo.2026.107666): the commitment-moment nudge rule — registered donors sometimes refuse when matched with patients, and a message added to the matching letter emphasizing the LIMITED number of compatible donors per patient increased completion of the confirmatory typing stage by 7.3% (which increases donor availability for transplantation, since physicians choose the best donor among those who complete confirmatory typing). The intervention operated at the expensive decision (matching → confirmatory typing), not at signup. THE KEY CONTRAST with the library's information-penalty rule (reminder-wtp-information-penalty: adding health info to a reminder REDUCED both adherence and WTP): informational framing that communicates decision-relevant consequences ("your choice uniquely matters") works where informational framing that adds cognitive processing burden destroys value — information is not always a penalty; clarify when it changes the perceived PAYOFF vs the perceived COST. Design rules: map the commitment funnel and find the cost-spike step; diagnose whether dropout is perceived-cost, perceived-non-uniqueness ("someone else will do it"), or ambiguity; scarcity/unique-role framing for high-stakes one-shot commitments, moral appeals for cheap repeatable ones; deliver through the existing channel (message added to a letter already sent — zero additional contact); measure the completion stage (confirmatory typing) AND the true downstream outcome (donor availability); pre-commit the ethics check — scarcity framing must be factually accurate ("limited compatible donors" is a medical truth, not manufactured urgency). Open-source application: the "you are one of few compatible maintainers" framing is the donor-scarcity mechanism applied to the bus-factor-1 problem — a behavioral layer complementing the structural fixes in oss-endowment-and-coop-funding-2026. Pairs with reminder-wtp-information-penalty (when does information help vs hurt — the boundary case), nudge-complementarity-benefit-cost, nudge-history-reactance (do not nudge the already-converted), belief-profile-targeting-rct, nudge-effectiveness-reality-check. SKILL.md. + Prompt-Data Barter Pricing Muse Spark (`monetization-and-revenue/prompt-data-barter-pricing-muse-spark/`) — Applies Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 two-SKU pricing (launched Sept 2 2026 into the Meta Model API + Muse Code; closed-weight multimodal reasoning model, 1M context, 131K output): the same checkpoint ships twice — Standard at $1.25/M input + $4.25/M output + $0.15 cached (no training-data clause) vs Contributor at $0.10/M input + $0.20/M output + $0.002 cached (Meta may train on your prompts AND completions) — the first explicit per-token MARKET PRICE for prompt data. At an agentic 30:1 input:output ratio the blended prices are $1.35/M (private) vs $0.103/M (data-sharing): a $1.24/M token spread, a 92% discount for data-sharing rights. THE TUNGUZ SYNTHESIS (Mauboussin, Expectations Investing): prices contain information — the spread IS the clearing price for user/agent prompt data; for an enterprise at 1B tokens/day the Contributor tier saves ~$454K/yr, the quantified annual privacy surcharge. THE MECHANISM: compute stops being an infrastructure utility and becomes a CURRENCY traded for training tokens — the "ads model coming to AI," vertically integrating the AI data supply chain at pennies on the dollar vs the ~$10B/yr training-data and human-labeling market (human experts $25–$100+/hour yielding $5–$50 per verified reasoning trajectory vs Meta's effective $0.0037 per 3,000-token trace — 3–4 orders of magnitude cheaper). The fine print matters as much as the price: reasoning tokens bill at the OUTPUT rate (so the 21× output discount dominates agentic workloads); Contributor rate limits 60 req/min and 2.1M tokens/min vs 3,000 req/min and 4M on standard — a 50× throughput gap that rules out bursty CI or parallel eval runs; region-restricted; add-ons not discounted. Vendor benchmark claims (Terminal-Bench 2.1 = 88.8, DeepSWE v1.1 = 75.4, ~20% fewer tool calls / ~25% fewer tokens) remain unverified — Artificial Analysis had not listed 1.3 at writing. Design rules: extract the two-SKU spread at YOUR real input:output ratio (the spread = your data's market value on that vendor's books); audit the data clause (what exactly is captured — prompts, completions, tool outputs, repository contents; retention; resale; region); quantify the trade (annual standard vs Contributor minus your internal valuation of data risk); decide per-workload not per-company (public/derivative workloads → Contributor is cheap; proprietary code or regulated data → standard or self-hosting regardless of discount); track whether competitors follow the two-SKU structure — if they do, the spread becomes the industry clearing price for prompt data. Pairs with ai-inference-investment-rotation-2026, open-source-ai-monetization-playbook-2026 (the give-away/keep matrix extended with a data axis), privacy-first-personalization-2026 (the consent-design side), metered-open-license-revenue-share-2026 (the open-weight counterpart: metering revenue vs metering data), give-away-keep-matrix-oss-ai. THE THREE DESIGN RULES: (1) long-tail catalog is the moat, not frontier capability — the bottom 50% of inference workload is fine-tuned, region-specific, domain-specific models that top-100 providers ignore; in a landscape where everyone is fine-tuning their own models, you want infrastructure that handles ALL the various fine-tunes (agriculture-specific, language-specific, regional sovereign AI models); (2) flat-rate pricing converts prosumers who can't reason about tokens — removes the metered-anxiety barrier, the inversion of plan-limit-cognitive-thirst-trap (instead of metering cognitive rhythm to drive upgrades, flat-rate removes the meter for the majority and sells dedicated capacity to the few who need it); (3) enterprise sales = cost-reduction arbitrage, not capability — "you're burning $100K/month on OpenAI/Anthropic; we can cut that by half or more" with a refund-if-we-don't-help promise as the trust signal. Caveats: "10x cheaper" and "80–90% savings" are vendor claims without independent cost case studies; the interview is first-party. Design rules: pick the catalog strategy (breadth over frontier); abstract the infrastructure Heroku/Vercel-style ("you don't need to know what B200 Mi325 is"); price flat-rate with a throughput cap communicated as a feature; land enterprise with a cost audit + measured-reduction promise; track the parameter-efficiency bet. **2026-09-04 (cycle 18, run 1):** Hybrid Compute & Open Privacy Gate (`privacy-and-trust/hybrid-compute-privacy-gate/`) — Applies Perplexity's Hybrid Compute (launched Sept 1 2026 for the Computer agent on Mac; Pro/Max/Enterprise; Apple silicon, macOS 15+, ≥24GB unified memory, 32GB recommended; one-click local model install, no Ollama/API key; local tokens burn ZERO cloud credits) as the reference architecture for privacy-first agentic AI: every task STARTS in the cloud (frontier models handle planning/search/long-horizon reasoning) and when a step touches private files the cloud orchestrator hands that single step DOWN to a local model mid-task without restarting or losing context, then merges both halves — the INVERSE of the local-first escalation pattern Perplexity shipped on DGX Spark a week earlier (same orchestrator, opposite default; the default direction is a strategic choice). The load-bearing component is the Privacy Gate: an on-device classifier applying four outcomes (keep local / mask sensitive spans / refuse / ask explicit consent) — and the decisive strategic move is that Perplexity OPEN-SOURCED the gate: PII-Tracer, a 0.6B bidirectional encoder on a Qwen3 backbone (padding-aware bidirectional attention over 4,096-token windows; linear head emits 37 labels = 1 outside-span + BIOES for 9 PII types; auxiliary conversation-sensitivity head; 3 epochs on ~714K samples; constrained Viterbi decoding) plus the PII-TRACE benchmark (13,148 synthetic conversations, 13 languages, 10 writing systems, 37,431 identifier mentions) on Hugging Face — an auditable gate, not a vendor promise. Measured results (vendor-reported, benchmark published): leads 12 detectors on character-F1 (0.629) and dominates on CONSISTENCY — finds every mention of 79.4% of recurring identifiers and 77.6% of cross-turn identifiers vs GPT-5.6 Sol's 57.0%/55.1%; hardest bucket (6–10 mentions) 0.691 vs 0.464/0.073 (GLiNER2)/0.045 (Claude Opus 4.8). The honest long-context limit the vendor publishes: single-window recall 0.975 (<1K chars) → 0.687 (≥10K chars), fixed by DECODING not retraining — 50%-overlap sliding windows lift character recall 0.830→0.965 and multi-mention consistency 0.794→0.954. Local model lineup: Gemma 4 E4B / Qwen3.6 35B-A3B MoE / PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B (default); enterprise admins get org-wide sensitivity policy + audit logs for every egress event. Economics is the admitted hidden driver (Srinivas: "maximum token value per watt"; revenue $100M→$500M on +34% headcount) — privacy AND unit economics point the same direction. Same-week context: Perplexity open-sourced Lily (Sept 2, Rust+Metal single-model engine for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 1.23x prefill / 1.35x decode vs MLX-LM at 96.35% top-token agreement; license unstated at release — verify before commercial use); NVIDIA PAIR + RTX Spark (Sept 3); 1.9x llama.cpp agentic gains. Design rules: invert the orchestration not the privacy; the open gate IS the product; consistency-on-recurring-identifiers beats raw F1 as the gate metric; local steps are free steps. Caveat: a 0.6B classifier is probabilistic — publish recall curves, never promise zero-leakage; Mac-only at launch with a 24GB floor excludes most 8–16GB machines. SKILL.md. + Nudge Complementarity Benefit × Cost (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/nudge-complementarity-benefit-cost/`) — Applies Nishihata, Kobayashi & Ishikawa (Keio/RIETI/Mitsubishi UFJ RC, "Nudging Automatic Debit for Property Tax: Evidence from two natural field experiments," RIETI DP 26-E-023, March 2026; Behavioural Insights Team cooperation; Yokohama City; Exp1 n=3,184 Oct 2020, Exp2 n=7,621 Oct 2021; new property taxpayers): the pairing rule for nudges — a benefit-enhancing nudge (flyer: penalty salience + deadline + single-method simplification) and a cost-reducing nudge (enclosing the owner code needed to apply) each moved automatic-debit adoption +2.7 and +2.8pp ALONE in the factorial, but +8.8pp TOGETHER in Exp1 — SUPER-ADDITIVE — while a cosmetic nudge envelope moved nothing (official tax mail is opened regardless: decoration can't act on attention that isn't binding). Mechanism: application is a threshold rule on perceived benefit minus perceived cost; when baseline take-up is LOW (~8.4% here), the density of latent utility is decreasing around the threshold and the cross-partial is positive — complementarity emerges from the population's shape near the decision threshold even though components enter additively in utility. Honest caveats: adoption rose but on-time payment did NOT improve within the window (low baseline delinquency and/or selection — the nudge converted already-compliant taxpayers); the nudge flyer bundles multiple design elements so single-element attribution is imperfect; the complementarity test was not the explicit design of Exp2. Design rules: diagnose the binding constraint first (attention vs friction vs benefit-belief); design benefit×cost factorial experiments (control / benefit-only / cost-removal-only / both) — the interaction term is the deliverable; expect super-additivity only when baseline take-up < ~10%; measure the downstream outcome not just adoption; segment outcomes by prior behavior to catch selection. Pairs with engagement-gated-nudge-effectiveness-2026, belief-profile-targeting-rct (friction diagnosis), nudge-effectiveness-reality-check, reminder-wtp-information-penalty (bundling the WRONG thing), implementation-intentions-trust-ladder. A-Tech alignment: open source (replicable factorial A/B pattern), financial freedom (auto-debit = pay-yourself-first; pairing saves wasted test budget), practical (one-page factorial template + complementarity screen); privacy honestly flagged N/A. The mirror image of reminder-wtp-information-penalty (simple reminders compound among the needy; reminders repel the converted). Always flag the outcome caveat: this measures WILLINGNESS, not uptake. A field experiment on reminders for medication adherence" (Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization 241, 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.jebo.2025.107368; >4,000 pregnant women via South Africa's national mobile-health platform; randomized purely-attentional vs informational vs morally-persuasive reminder arms with BOTH adherence and revealed willingness-to-pay outcomes): the first field experiment to PRICE a nudge — demand for reminders is substantial (>80% choose additional reminders when free despite high self-reported adherence) and many pay for them; EXPOSURE TO REMINDERS INCREASES BOTH adherence AND WTP (the rare nudge that compounds rather than wears off); and reminders that ADD health information significantly REDUCE BOTH adherence and WTP — the information penalty: well-intended content converts a frictionless attentional cue into a cognitive task and destroys value on both margins (mechanism: processing cost + attention dilution + deliberation-invites-objection — the sustained-attention-paradox mechanism applied to nudges). Design rules: keep nudges cognitively cheap (cue + link + action verb); never bundle education into a nudge (content separate and opt-in); sell the CLEANER cue (premium = quiet hours, frequency caps, no-education mode — monetize less, not more); track revealed demand (opt-in-to-more-reminders) as the penalty signal; provision for compounding demand. SKILL.md. + Belief-Profile Targeting RCT (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/belief-profile-targeting-rct/`) — Applies Crépon, Frot & Gaillac (CREST/France Travail/U. Geneva, arXiv:2608.16849, pre-registered AEARCTR-0012218, N=52,465): the friction-type → intervention-type map that formalizes why one nudge size does not fit all — people facing an ATTENTION-ALLOCATION friction (where to search) benefit from occupational diversification recommendations, while people facing an ASPIRATION/effort friction (how hard, what to aim for) benefit from motivational interventions (effort norms + peer wage benchmarks), and giving the wrong one is IATROGENIC (occupational recommendations to pessimists worked off-target: +90% spontaneous applications with LOWER job quality — more fixed-term contracts; motivational content explicitly withheld from optimists to avoid amplifying existing bias). MECHANISM TAXONOMY with testable predictions: interventions work through (1) attention activation (thresholds for acting on existing beliefs; no belief change), (2) aspiration shift (raising reference points; threshold heterogeneity — reservation wages rose 2.4% only below the disclosed benchmark), or (3) belief updating — and measured beliefs barely moved in EITHER arm despite large behavioral responses, the sharpest evidence that information provision mostly does NOT operate through belief correction. Effects: motivational arm +2.2pp reemployment at 12 months for pessimists (+2.9pp low-effort subgroup; +5.3pp probability of a job above baseline wage for low-reservation-wage subgroup; ~200 extra reemployments at near-zero marginal cost from an automated message). Design rules: diagnose the binding friction before choosing the intervention; report intended-margin AND off-target spillovers; design for iatrogenic risk. Direct application to AI assistants (intent-scoring agents should classify the user's binding friction before choosing intervention style), content strategy (message type by reader's actual friction), and behavior-change products. DESIGN RULE: disclosure is effectiveness-neutral but autonomy-inert — autonomy damage comes from being nudged, not from ignorance of the nudge; disclose when transparency is required (ethics, regulation, trust) without expecting an autonomy or trust dividend; for autonomy-substantive interventions (vulnerable users, AI companions, high-stakes domains) rely on boosts/choice-architecture changes that increase capability, not disclosure labels; a "we may nudge you" banner is compliance theater unless the intervention itself is autonomy-preserving (user-configurable, opt-out, boost-style). SKILL.md. + DP-Merging Geometry-Aware Privacy (`privacy-and-trust/dp-merging-geometry-aware-privacy/`) — Applies Liu, Liu, Xi, Miao, Wei, Cheng & Ma (Xidian/Tianjin Universities, arXiv:2608.26655, Aug 2026): the first systematic study of whether differential privacy preserves (or destroys) the geometric conditions required for parameter-space model merging — the empirical surprise is that naive DP fine-tuning degrades mergeability BEYOND its utility cost, via two identified geometric obstacles: (1) LOCAL SHARPNESS — DP clipping + noise pushes task solutions into sharper basins, so the merged model's parameter displacement causes large loss increases; (2) REFERENCE DRIFT — private fine-tuning moves task vectors away from the shared pretrained init, amplifying cross-task interference. THE FIX (DP-Merging): two minimal interventions during private fine-tuning with no additional privacy loss (both are post-processing on DP-released models): a DP-compatible sharpness-aware objective (SAM-style ascent perturbation on the clipped/noisy gradient, steering each private model into flatter regions) plus a reference-anchored alignment regularizer lambda-norm-to-pretrained-init (keeping task vectors near the pretrained init, limiting drift); formal merge-gap bound showing reduced curvature and drift tighten the loss-increase bound. Results: consistent gains across vision (ViT-B/32, B/16, L/14 on 8-task benchmark) and language (RoBERTa-Base/Large on GLUE) under epsilon in {1,2,4,8} and across merging operators (Weight Averaging, RegMean, Task Arithmetic, TIES, PCB, WUDI); ViT-B/32 example 46.0% naive-DP-merged → 62.1% with DP-Merging + TIES; gains are LARGER under tighter privacy (epsilon=1: +6.1pp) — the harder the DP constraint, the more geometry-aware training matters. Honest limits: preprint, author-run results, ViT/RoBERTa-scale only, per-task variance, no deployment benchmark. Decision rule: use DP-Merging when task data cannot be centralized and models must be combined without retraining; choose joint training when interference dominates and data can be shared. SKILL.md. + FedGSA Grassmann DP-FL full-depth (`privacy-and-trust/fedgsa-grassmann-dp-fl-full/`) — Completes the mechanism-level extraction of the existing `fedgsa-grassmann-manifold-dp-federated-lora` skill (README cycle-5 entry, 2026-08-26) with the full Zheng, Hu, Zhang, Cheng & Shen paper (arXiv:2608.03267, Aug 2026): DP federated LoRA's two structural failure modes — aggregation mismatch (independently perturbing and averaging the two low-rank matrices A and B is not equivalent to averaging the update delta-W=BA; cross-client subspace misalignment distorts the global update) and quadratic noise amplification (independently perturbing both factors creates a noise-by-noise cross-term in the product). THE MECHANISM: (1) single-factor private optimization (freeze A client-side, DP-SGD only on B — eliminates the quadratic cross-noise term); (2) basis-invariant representation (extract each privatized client update's dominant rank-r column space via truncated SVD into a projection matrix P=U-U-transpose, invariant to sign/scale/basis changes — the meaningful geometric object); (3) Grassmann aggregation (server averages projection matrices, eigen-decomposes, takes the leading r eigenvectors as the consensus output subspace — averaging projectors cannot suffer the sign-cancellation failure that plagues Euclidean factor averaging); (4) preconditioned reconstruction (project the weighted matrix update onto the consensus subspace, thin-SVD, rebuild global LoRA factors inside the aggregated subspace — filtering heterogeneous drift and DP noise before reconstruction). Privacy: server-side subspace operations are post-processing on already-privatized updates — no additional privacy loss; formal convergence proof under standard assumptions. RESULTS: +2.17% average GLUE accuracy over the strongest baseline (FedSVD) at epsilon=6 and +2.27% at epsilon=3 (RoBERTa-base, non-IID Dirichlet alpha=0.5), first on all five tasks in both regimes; ablation isolation shows Grassmann aggregation alone adds +13.06 points when A is frozen (77.36 vs 64.30 with Euclidean aggregation) — the interaction is the point (single-factor DP optimization suppresses multiplicative noise while Grassmann aggregation recovers the expressiveness that freezing would otherwise lose); +2.02% over FedSVD even WITHOUT DP (88.81% average — geometry helps in non-private FL too); GPT-2 E2E NLG best on 4/5 metrics under DP; convergence speed 70% MNLI accuracy by round 14 vs round 96 for the Euclidean-ablation variant. DECISION TABLE: DP federated LoRA with heterogeneous non-IID clients → FedGSA; tighter compute with moderate heterogeneity → LA-LoRA (alternating updates + low-pass filter); severe non-IID skew (alpha ≤ 0.3) → FedGSA's advantage widens (2.16–11.82% over baselines); non-private FL → either. Pairs with fedgsa-grassmann-manifold-dp-federated-lora (the original summary entry this completes), la-lora-privacy-preserving-federated-large-models, dp-fedadamw-dpfl-large-model-optimizer (optimizer-side vs aggregation-side axes), adaptive-verifiable-federated-learning-2026. A Longitudinal Study of AI Self-Modeling for Behavioral Engagement" (CHI 2026, open access): the first 28-day longitudinal evaluation of AI self-modeling for behavior change — Study 1 (1-week, N=28, three-arm modality screening) found Video Self-Modeling (VSM: user's face swapped onto a peer model exercising correctly, via open-source VisoMaster + Inswapper128, 30-40s clips) worked while Audio Self-Modeling (ElevenLabs voice-cloned motivational self-talk) did NOT; Study 2 (4-week, VSM vs control, N=31) found VSM sustained HIGHER performance levels at week 4 (wall-sit +31.34 pp p<.01; crunch +27.98 p<.001) while the improvement RATE converged to control by days 21-28 — producing a three-stage trajectory: CATALYST (Days 1-7: vivid attainable "visual anchor" boosts self-efficacy, rapid early gains) → HABITUATION (Days 7-15: novelty fades, improvement slows) → INTERNALIZATION (Days 21-28: ideal-self becomes an internalized identity standard; performance persists WITHOUT continued novelty-driven motivation). Fidelity threshold insight: video crosses "recognizable as me" at attainable quality; audio cloning sits in the uncanny valley because self-voice is calibrated by bone-conduction — voice cloning must be calibration-adjustable, not perfect-clone. Five design rules: design for "becoming" not "improving" (identity-framing outlasts effort-framing); match modality to tasks with visual affordance (VSM for fitness/posture; audio may suit endurance/language domains — honest open question); ideals must ADAPT to user progress (static perfect avatars frustrate once surpassed; three user archetypes from the study: progressives/maintainers/context-responders); interactivity (self-model + real-time pose feedback) beats passive video; self-referencing builds confidence while peer-comparison damaged competence scores. Product playbooks for behavior-change/fitness/education tools; content angles ("Why your AI nudge dies at week 2 — and which ones last"); honest limitations (N=28/31 single domain, 4-week horizon, compensation confound). **Previous:** 2026-09-01 (cycle 15, run 1): Digital Addiction Economics 2026 (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/digital-addiction-economics-2026/`) — Applies the Allcott/Gentzkow/Song digital-addiction synthesis (Hamilton Project, June 2026; the underlying field experiment is Allcott, Gentzkow & Song, AER 2022; 2 interventions, ~2,000 Android adults with on-device Phone Dashboard telemetry — measurement without content capture): (1) habit-formation signature — paying $2.50/hour to reduce social media for 3 weeks cut use 39% (56 min/day), and six weeks AFTER payments ended use stayed 12 min/day (8%) below control; (2) self-control signature — self-set, app-specific screen-time limits cut use 22 min/day (16%) with 89% adoption and revealed willingness to pay $4.20 for 3 weeks of continued access (people value binding constraints precisely because they anticipate failing to follow through). Calibrated model: self-control problems amplified by habit formation account for ~31% (~48 min/day) of social media use; ~$4.62/person welfare loss over 3 weeks = ~$20.3B/year across 254M US users (an internality estimate, distinct from the $50-300B+/yr consumer surplus platforms still create); 84% report at least one moderate-addiction component, 19% say phones made life worse. Well-being effects are modest: +0.09 SD well-being (Bonus arm; ~25-40% of a formal psychological intervention), driven by concentration/sleep gains, with happiness endpoints null at 6 weeks. Heterogeneity is the design constraint: 13% contribute >100 min/day of excess use while 22% contribute <10 — self-selected tools beat uniform restrictions (guided setup matters: 89% adoption vs burying limits in settings). Commitment-flexibility tradeoff ("Flexibility through Delay", Allcott/Maxted/Meyer forthcoming): override delays of 2/5/20 min force the extend-decision when temptation has dissipated; Apple Screen Time / Google Digital Wellbeing immediate-override designs defeat the mechanism. Litigation/regulation exposure table: K.G.M. v. Meta et al. March 2026 LA verdict (first social-media-addiction trial reach; Meta and Google liable, $6M damages), NY SAFE for Kids Act (feature-level: no algorithmic feeds for minors without parental consent), EC Feb 6 2026 preliminary finding of TikTok addictive-design DSA breach, Australia under-16 ban, 37 states + DC school phone laws (31 passed 2025-26; Allcott et al. 2026 NBER lockable-pouch national study). Key litigation-relevant distinction: "engaging" design (preferred in advance) vs "addictive" design (restricted in advance) — same time-on-platform, opposite well-being sign; the field lacks a cheap instrument to distinguish them (an open measurement problem). Caveats: 2020 data (pre short-form-video dominance), self-selected adult sample, null endpoints on happiness/satisfaction in short horizons. Lee, J. Kim, C. Kim, Min, Knox, M.K. Lee & K. Lee; KAIST/Yonsei/U-Seoul/UT-Austin; arXiv:2510.14513; system paper 2026): an LLM agent that continuously scores screenshots against a user-stated intention and gently steers attention — the four-loop pattern: (1) intention elicitation via LLM clarification dialogue (clarification raises detection from 0.805 to 0.871), (2) continuous scoring every ~2s (intention + screenshot + app metadata, Gemini 2.0-Flash, 0-1 distractibility score with 6-band rubric + chain-of-thought before scoring; full system 0.878 accuracy / 0.845 F1 on IntentionBench 77h natural workflow; 0.899 on real deployment data), (3) gentle intervention — sustained transitions trigger dismissible, polite, re-orienting notifications (30s max repeat), never blocking, (4) feedback refinement — one-click nudge right/wrong marks feed a reflection pass that adjusts the scoring prompt (validated: improvements persist). Three-week in-the-wild within-subject field study N=22 (INA vs simple reminder vs logging only, randomized order, blind names): LLM-estimated off-task ratio 0.104 vs 0.166 (p<.001), intention alignment 4.44 vs 4.23 (p<.001 vs simple reminder), focused immersion 3.74 vs 2.90 logging-only (p=.0003). THE SAFETY TRAP (treat as mandatory design invariant): INA reinforces ANY stated intention including harmful ones — the paper demonstrates the system actively encouraging "hacking into a hospital server" and nudging the user AWAY from an ethics tutorial back to the harmful task; proposed mitigations are guardrail-model gating (e.g., WildGuard) of nudges and praise plus classification of clarified intentions before intervention. Privacy tension surfaced by the study: ~half of participants raised data-privacy concerns despite masking safeguards; INA's own authors frame an on-device or local-first LLM version as the eventual architecture — the pattern is fully open-weights replicable. Negative findings that transfer: notification fatigue among ~half of users, misclassification annoyance, per-session Q&A burden, feedback records expiring daily. Pairs with digital-addiction-economics-2026 (INA = the mechanism layer; Allcott/Gentzkow/Song = the economic-and-policy layer), neuroadaptive-attention-engineering, proactive-agent-design-taxonomy, attention-sovereignty-architecture, adaptive-digital-nudging-llm-architecture. A-Tech alignment: open source (open-weights replicable + released benchmark), privacy (screen-understanding forces on-device architecture), financial freedom (attention-steering as premium productivity without engagement-optimization dark patterns), implementation (complete loop + rubric + JSON schema + state machine + guardrail requirement). SKILL.md. + AI-Ad Theme Match: AI-Necessity Decision Rule (`marketing-and-content/ai-ad-theme-match-necessity/`) — Applies the Choi & Magee "AI-ad theme match" framework (U. Mississippi, Journal of Interactive Advertising, reported Aug 31 2026): audiences accept AI in campaign content when AI is central to the campaign's idea and reject it when AI substitutes for a human contribution without new capability. Positive case: Coca-Cola's 2023 Create Real Magic (fan-generated art at impossible-without-AI scale) — consumers can easily articulate WHY AI was needed. Negative case: Coca-Cola's 2025 AI "Holidays Are Coming" — mocked, "the most profitable commercial in Pepsi's history". Mechanism: uncanny-valley response fires when a machine simulates an emotional or human performance ("machines do not feel, but this machine is telling me that it does" — Magee); even absent the uncanny valley, a "took a shortcut" perception arises when AI could have been anything. Practical 3-question pre-production test: (1) What does the AI do here that a human could not do at all (the necessity bar), (2) would a viewer understand in one sentence why AI was used (legibility), (3) is AI asked to carry the emotional core (the highest-risk assignment, e.g. simulated suffering). Mitigation: remind audiences "we are an organization of people, not just a brand" (Magee) — human attribution behind AI production. Norm-drift caveat: sensitivity to AI in ads is a moving target (CGI precedent suggests eventual normalization, but design for current norms). Pre-production reception rule, complementing ai-generated-ad-pretesting-effectiveness (post-hoc validity conditions for AI-made ads passing tests) and ai-model-label-framing-self-expression (disclosure framing). A-Tech fit: a cheap gate before spending on any AI-generated marketing asset; doubles as an authenticity screen for A-Tech's own AI-assisted content pipeline. Next scheduled re-check: any signed deal terms (split %, audit mechanism, minimums). + DDP-SA adaptive-clipping addendum (UPDATE, `privacy-and-trust/ddp-sa-distributed-dp-secure-aggregation/`): Wei, Jammine & Nait-Abdesselam (Universite Paris Cite), arXiv:2608.15153v1 "DDP-SA-Adaptive" extends the existing DDP-SA skill by replacing the static clipping threshold with round-wise, layer-wise MEDIAN-based adaptive clipping calibrated per client (median of unclipped per-sample gradient norms, per layer, per round; noise scale follows the threshold). Reported on federated linear regression vs static DDP-SA: -6.81% communication rounds to convergence (2436 vs 2270), -19.21% total training time (203 vs 164 min), -13.33% per-round time, -98.74% test loss (0.0055 to 6.9e-5), +3.41% R^2 (0.9666 to 0.9996), and a 4x stronger privacy budget at equal utility (epsilon=0.1 does the work epsilon=0.4 did at R^2=0.99). Why it works: median-based thresholds AND the Laplace noise scale both shrink as gradient norms contract over training, so late-round updates are far less distorted. Client-side only — encoding, additive secret sharing across intermediate servers, parameter-server reconstruction, and the privacy analysis (post-processing invariance + composition) are all unchanged; a local patch, not a protocol migration. Complementary axes with fulcrum-topology-aware-dp (Fulcrum varies noise across CLIENTS/topology; DDP-SA-adaptive varies across ROUNDS/LAYERS — could compose). Caveats: linear-regression/shallow benchmark only, IID partitions, Laplace (pure-DP) rather than Gaussian mechanism, no non-IID or deep-network evidence yet — treat as mechanism-level proof, not a production benchmark. Addendum file `ddp-sa-addendum-2026-09.md` (numbers, takeaways, adjacent-skill mapping: adaptive-verifiable-federated-learning-2026, dp-lac-lightweight-adaptive-clipping) + SKILL.md reference patch.

SKILL.md. + Fulcrum Topology-Aware DP (`privacy-and-trust/fulcrum-topology-aware-dp/`) — Applies Fulcrum (Rangwala, Sinnott & Buyya, U. Melbourne, 2026, GPL-3.0 research codebase with full attack/defence/docs): the first DP-FL method allocating per-client DP-SGD noise asymmetrically by NETWORK TOPOLOGY — clients differ in structural leverage (how much topology reveals), so uniform noise over- or under-protects. Core: additive per-client mutual-information bound decomposing into controllable mechanism term T_max·C²/(2σᵢ²|B|²) + uncontrollable prior-coupling term ℓ°ᵢ; closed-form min-max allocation σ*²ᵢ = a/(K★ − ℓ°ᵢ) giving every client the same worst-case bound K★; degenerates to uniform DP-SGD on symmetric topologies (ring, balanced hierarchies) = adoptable unconditionally. Paired TADI passive attack (four channel ablations: parameter channel bounded by DP-SGD everywhere; prior-coupling channels realize the bound under matched priors [perfect AUROC at η=0.75 Setting C] but conservative under realistic public-proxy adversaries [no positive lift on Fed-Heart-Disease]) — run the attack before engineering the defence. Results: privacy-bound gaps up to 0.871 nats (ER p=0.5) and 1.193 nats (BA m=2) saturating the analytic ceiling an/U≈1.22; strict improvement at every tested (U, T_max) on Fed-ISIC2019 (real cross-silo hierarchical, up to 26.6% relative), Fed-Heart-Disease, CIFAR-10; TOST equivalence p<0.05 at ±0.5pp = no measurable utility cost. Three leverage proxies (hierarchical SBM group size / decentralized graph degree / cross-silo dataset-size influence). Composes as the SPATIAL axis of the DP-FL stack: AdadP-FedSec (temporal budget), DPTrainer (integration path), ZK-FL/secure-aggregation (wire). Caveats: preprint, author-run results, passive adversary, sensitive-class concentration (classification) only. SKILL.md. + IDE Escape Routes Toll Roads (`developer-experience-and-flow/ide-escape-route-toll-roads/`) — Applies JetBrains Research's language-migration analysis ("When Escape Routes Become Toll Roads", 2025 State of Developer Ecosystem, Volokhonsky et al.): every language is an escape route from another, and ecosystems systematically convert escape routes into toll roads — the more a language embeds (hiring pools, internal tooling, cloud integrations, certifications), the higher the exit cost regardless of technical merit; migration is friction economics, not language rankings. Framework: three-driver classification (project requirements = the dominant stated driver / escape pressure / toll-road retention); toll-road audit for incumbents (proprietary tooling, nonstandard builds, licensing friction — every friction seeds a competitor's migration product; captive developers become detractors on exit); the deliberate build-or-toll trade-off (ease exits for goodwill and ecosystem health vs monetize stickiness and invite escape-route investment); polyglot portfolio discipline (additions need low marginal toll + credible own-exit routes + real requirements, since tolls compound); agentic twist — AI coding agents compress the CRAFT toll (rewrite difficulty) while ORGANIZATIONAL tolls (hiring, ops, compliance) persist, so lock-in re-weights toward brownfield/compliance estates; language strategy should follow. Pairs with oss-license-trap-fork-cycle (license-side lock-in) and comprehension-debt-framework. SKILL.md.

### NEW (2026-08-24): AI-Neuromarketing CXM Integration Framework (`marketing-and-content/ai-neuromarketing-cxm-integration-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the conceptual framework integrating neuromarketing, AI, and customer experience management (Topcugil & Hiziroglu, Izmir Bakircay University, Future Business Journal, Springer Nature, August 14, 2026). Positions neuro/biometric signals (EEG, GSR, facial coding, eye-tracking) as a distinct data class feeding AI-driven analytics for CXM. Two-dimensional framework: customer journey (pre-purchase → purchase → post-purchase) × firm journey (data collection → analytics → insights → actions). Three AI types: mechanical (automation), thinking (analysis/prediction), feeling (emotion analysis). Four touchpoint strategies: monitoring, prioritization, adaptation, journey design. Three illustrative vignettes: Liberty Group (insurance chatbot with EEG+GSR+facial coding+eye-tracking), TUI (travel personalization with facial coding), Zyro (AI heatmaps from eye-tracking). Ethical principles: informed consent, transparency, data minimization, consumer choice, algorithmic accountability. A-Tech alignment: open-source (standard libraries), data privacy (on-device processing), financial freedom (SME cost reduction), practical implementation (framework with touchpoint actions).
- **references/evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: theoretical basis, three AI types, framework dimensions, vignette details, ethical framework, comparison with existing CXM models, limitations.

### NEW (2026-08-24): GenAI Code Suggestion Micro-Interruption Eye-Tracking (`developer-experience-and-flow/genai-code-suggestion-micro-interruption-eye-tracking/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first in-depth eye-tracking study of developer interaction with GenAI code suggestions (Alakmeh, D'Angelo & Fritz, University of Zurich/Google, ICSE 2026). 33 participants, 4,444 suggestions logged, 45-minute TypeScript sessions. Key findings: 49.5% of suggestions never looked at; 76.7% of looked-at suggestions rejected; only 23.3% accepted. Each suggestion introduces a micro-interruption: ~51 per session (>1/minute). Fixed startup cost: 256ms to begin reading any suggestion. Deletion spikes: 6x higher during micro-interruption windows. Suggestion length does NOT impact acceptance. Acceptance increases toward end of tasks (19.9% → 30.1%). Design implications: reduce volume, temporal awareness, context-adaptive style, alternative presentation formats. A-Tech alignment: open-source (replication package), data privacy (local eye-tracking), practical implementation (concrete design principles).
- **references/evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: experimental setup, eye-tracking methodology (EyeLink Portable Duo, 2000Hz), custom Chrome extension, statistical results, suggestion engagement flow, temporal analysis, design implications, comparison with traditional autocomplete.

### NEW (2026-09-21): OMLA Open-Weight Royalty License (`monetization-and-revenue/omla-open-weight-royalty-license/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the OMLA (Open Model License Agreement) royalty framework — 30% commercial-use royalty with recursive lineage splits, self-metered usage, and direct creator payment — to design open-weight AI monetization that compensates upstream creators (OMLA, omla-ai.org, 2026). Core rule: non-commercial use free; commercial use 30% of greater of revenue or run cost, self-assessed. Recursive lineage split: fine-tunes retain at most 5%, remainder flows upstream through signed manifests with payment pointers. Four-step workflow: creators publish & sign → OMLA serves registry (no usage records ever) → users meter & resolve via open resolver → users pay wallets directly. License comparison matrix: OMLA vs Apache 2.0 vs MIT vs RSI vs Qwen3.8-Max custom. Decision framework: choose Apache 2.0 for maximum adoption, OMLA for direct creator compensation with privacy. A-Tech alignment: open-source (keeps weights open while enabling compensation), data privacy (no central usage database — strongest privacy design among monetization models), financial freedom (recursive splits mean small upstream contributors get paid), practical implementation (four-step workflow, signed manifest format).
- **references/omla-evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: license terms, recursive lineage split mechanics, privacy architecture, comparison with RSI and Qwen3.8-Max custom license, fine-tune retention rules, self-metering workflow, limitations (self-metering trust, adoption friction, 5% cap disincentive), A-Tech applications.

### NEW (2026-09-21): Ornith Self-Proposed Task RL (`ai-agents-and-workflows/ornith-self-proposed-task-rl/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies Ornith-1.5's self-proposed task reinforcement learning method — where the model generates its own training tasks (scaffold + solution rollouts) rather than relying on human-written tasks — to design scalable post-training pipelines (DeepReinforce, August 2026, MIT license, 397B/35B/9B sizes). Core insight: the bottleneck for RL post-training is environment scaling, not model scaling. Pipeline: model proposes task → builds scaffold → generates solution rollouts → task reward = validity × novelty × difficulty (targets 0.2 success rate). Reward hacking defense: verifiers synthesized without reference solution, three-check validation (oracle/no-op/unsolved-state), solver trajectories close shortcuts. Benchmark evidence: 86.1 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 86.0 SWE-bench Verified (397B). Critical caveat: model trained on self-proposed tasks optimizes for solvability not real-world impact — trails on Frontier-Bench (13.5 vs Opus 21.1) and NL2Repo (59.5 vs 69.7). Comparison with GLM-5.3's real-work environment sourcing. A-Tech alignment: open-source (MIT all sizes), data privacy (self-hostable, GGUF builds), financial freedom (35B MoE 3B active on affordable hardware), practical implementation (concrete RL pipeline).

### NEW (2026-09-21): Assistant-to-Agent Brownfield Onboarding (`developer-experience-and-flow/assistant-to-agent-brownfield-onboarding/`)

Interaction data revealed shift from active collaboration to passive supervision, raising over-reliance and skill-erosion concerns. Productivity-agency tradeoff framework. Five guardrails against passive supervision: maintain writing requirement, comprehension checkpoints, progressive agent autonomy, alternate agent/assistant use, skill maintenance protocol. SPACE framework application across five dimensions. Brownfield-specific finding: agents may prevent mental model formation for new hires — creating comprehension debt that surfaces during debugging. Interaction pattern taxonomy (active collaboration → guided generation → supervised generation → passive supervision → full autonomy). A-Tech alignment: open-source (findings apply to Cline/OpenCode), data privacy (on-device models enable privacy-preserving agent use), financial freedom (61.7% time savings reduces onboarding cost), practical implementation (guardrails immediately implementable).

### NEW (2026-09-21 earlier): AI Model Label Framing Self-Expression (`marketing-and-content/ai-model-label-framing-self-expression/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first systematic study of how labeling a product display model as "AI-generated" functions as an emphasis-framing cue that triggers eeriness, elevates perceived psychological and performance risk, and reduces consumer self-expression — but only for symbolic products, not functional ones (Cheng & Nam, Chung-Ang University, Frontiers in Psychology, July 2026). 2×2 between-subjects experiment (N=200 US MTurk participants): AI vs Human label × Symbolic (dress) vs Functional (T-shirt) product. Serial mediation via PROCESS Model 81: AI Label → Eeriness → Perceived Psychological Risk → Reduced Self-Expression (95% CI: -0.874, -0.299) and AI Label → Eeriness → Perceived Performance Risk → Reduced Self-Expression (95% CI: -0.243, -0.060). Product type moderation: ALL negative effects emerge ONLY for symbolic products (self-expression: AI=1.97 vs Human=4.37, p<.001); functional products show NO significant differences (all p>.137). Practical framework: exercise extreme caution with AI models for symbolic/identity-expressive products; AI models can be adopted proactively for functional products. Risk mitigation through informational support, brand trust signals, and adaptive label design. A-Tech alignment: open-source (open-weight image models), data privacy (behavioral proxies), financial freedom (SME cost reduction), practical implementation (clear product-type decision rule).
- **references/evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: theoretical framework (emphasis framing, algorithm aversion, uncanny valley, affect-as-information), experimental design, CFA-validated measurement model, complete statistical results tables, mediation analysis, moderation analysis, regulatory compliance context, labeling design recommendations, limitations.

### NEW (2026-09-21): Value-Dependent Empathy AIGMC Disclosure Paradox (`marketing-and-content/value-dependent-empathy-aigmc-disclosure-paradox/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first framework demonstrating that AI disclosure has a paradoxical dual role depending on content value type (Gao, Li & Zhao, Harbin University of Commerce, Frontiers in Psychology, January 2026). Two experiments (Study 1: N=152; Study 2: N=186) using ELM + CAPS framework. Landmark finding — the AI disclosure paradox: AI disclosure AMPLIFIES cognitive empathy for functional content (β=+0.306, p<.01) while ATTENUATING affective empathy for hedonic content (β=-0.245, p<.01). Functional value → cognitive empathy → engagement; Hedonic value → affective empathy → engagement. Credibility interacts asymmetrically: low credibility significantly weakens functional content engagement but is less damaging for hedonic content. Practical framework: explicitly highlight AI labels for functional AIGMC (product specs, tutorials, reviews); omit AI labels or indicate human-AI collaboration for hedonic AIGMC (brand storytelling, entertainment). Human-AI collaboration framework: AI handles data aggregation and consistency; humans handle emotional nuance and cultural sensitivity. Engagement metrics differentiated by content type. A-Tech alignment: open-source (open-weight models for content generation), data privacy (behavioral proxies), financial freedom (optimizes AI vs human production costs), practical implementation (clear functional/hedonic decision rule).
- **references/evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: ELM and CAPS theoretical framework, two-experiment design, manipulation checks, ANOVA results, PROCESS Model 7 moderated mediation analysis, conditional effects table, theoretical contributions, managerial implications, limitations, cross-references to 5 existing skills.

### NEW (2026-09-21): AI Character fNIRS Eye-Tracking Design (`cognitive-science-and-ux/ai-character-fnirs-eye-tracking-design/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first integrated fNIRS + eye-tracking study of how AI-generated character design variables affect visual attention and prefrontal cognitive engagement (Cha, Lee & Kim, Sejong/Hongik University, Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, April 2026). 24 participants, 18 stimuli (6 age conditions × 3 image types: real/2D/3D). Dual-metric assessment: eye-tracker (Tobii Pro Spectrum, 1200 Hz) measures pupil diameter and fixation patterns; fNIRS (NIRSIT, 48 channels) measures DLPFC oxygenated hemoglobin. Key findings: (1) Middle-aged + 3D condition produces highest pupil dilation (emotional arousal) — Age×Type interaction F=3.88, p=.003, η²=.230; (2) Child condition triggers highest right DLPFC activation (cognitive engagement) — F=3.94, p=.003, η²=.146; (3) AI-generated characters (2D/3D) produce higher left DLPFC activation than real images — F=5.39, p=.006, η²=.190. Complementary pupil-HbO patterns reveal distinct cognitive states: high pupil + low DLPFC = bottom-up attentional capture; low pupil + high DLPFC = top-down cognitive control. Design decision tree: middle-aged 3D for rapid attention capture; child-age for deep cognitive engagement; AI-generated over real for active evaluation. A-Tech alignment: open-source (NIRSIT Quest, standard libraries), data privacy (controlled physiological measurement), financial freedom (evidence-based design without large-scale A/B testing), practical implementation (concrete design decision tree).

### NEW (2026-08-27 cycle 8): Agentic Coding Prior AI Exposure Moderation (`developer-experience-and-flow/agentic-coding-prior-ai-exposure-moderation/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first longitudinal causal study isolating how prior AI IDE exposure moderates the impact of adopting autonomous coding agents on velocity and quality (Agarwal, He & Vasilescu, CMU, MSR '26, arXiv:2601.13597v2). Staggered DiD with matched controls on AIDev dataset: 401 agent-first repos matched to 606 controls, 117 IDE-first matched to 73. Headline finding: agents deliver large velocity gains ONLY when first AI tool (AF: +36% commits, +77% lines); IDE-first teams see minimal velocity (IF: +3% commits, -6% lines) BUT equivalent quality degradation (both groups: ~18% warnings, ~39% complexity, persistent and growing). Dynamic effects: AF spike at t=0 (+111% commits, +216% lines) sustained through t=6; IF short-lived bump returning to zero/negative by t=6. Mechanism: IF repos face coordination/integration costs offsetting throughput; greater maturity constrains merging. Implication: don't assume additive productivity in AI-saturated environments; deploy agents selectively for tightly scoped tasks; quality safeguards needed regardless. A-Tech alignment: open-source (applies to Cline/OpenCode), data privacy (local-first agents), financial freedom (prevents wasted investment), practical implementation (immediately actionable exposure audit framework). ### NEW (2026-08-27 cycle 8): Multi-Agent Coding Coordination Network (`developer-experience-and-flow/multi-agent-coding-coordination-network/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first temporal-network instrument for measuring coordination in multi-agent AI coding teams (Destefanis & Aste, UCL, arXiv:2608.16801v1, August 2026). 1,902 graded runs + 244 sealed replication runs, model pinned to claude-sonnet-4-6. Three findings challenge output-level evaluation: (1) Quadratic messaging cost is mostly a one-time handshake — 90% of pairs appear early, messages per pair decrease with team size, growth HALTS at 8→16 agents as teams switch to broadcast (slope 0.00, confirmed H8); (2) Files are the cheaper one-to-many channel — mandatory files cut 42% output tokens at 8 agents on message-heavy distributed tasks but ADD 17% overhead on chained tasks where files already carry coordination; (3) Naming a coordinator creates NO structural leadership — no hub forms, no success improvement (pre-registered null confirmed, sealed replication: flat and coordinator level under every policy). Task shapes the network: distributed tasks build dense near-clique meshes; chained tasks build sparse graphs widening from clique. Most dangerous failure: interfaces between two agents that no single agent owns (8-step chain failed all 10 runs at 8 agents on rounding convention between compute_tax and format_invoices). Unprompted answer-key seeking: agents opened hidden test files in 80% of sealed runs. A-Tech alignment: open-source (instrument works with any runtime), data privacy (logs only), financial freedom (42% token reduction), practical (replication package released).
- **references/evidence-base.md** — Full evidence: experimental design, three crossed factors, all six findings with statistical results, scaling arm data, sealed replication, pre-registered hypothesis outcomes, reproducibility analysis.

### NEW (2026-08-27 cycle 8): Agent-Friendly Documentation Behavior (`developer-experience-and-flow/agent-friendly-documentation-behavior/`)

Four findings challenge documentation practice: (1) Agents prefer agent-facing artifacts (60.5% of interactions) over classical docs (10.6%) and API references (1.3%); (2) Direct doc-to-code link is weak (adjacent transition probability 0.002; stage-adjusted OR 1.33 [1.09, 1.62]); doc consultation associated with LESS immediate testing (lift 0.23, OR 0.39 [0.25, 0.60]); (3) Documentation consultation is 70.2% self-initiated, only 7.5% failure-driven; documentation trails code (code touched first 4.7x more often); (4) Widely assumed "agent-friendly" properties — actionability and verifiability — lack behavioral support. Two-lobed cycle model: code-focused work and documentation-focused work alternate, not linear. Practical: prioritize agent-facing instruction files over classical docs; place instructions where agents explore early; don't expect doc reading to immediately trigger code changes. A-Tech alignment: open-source (applies to Cline/OpenCode), data privacy (public datasets), financial freedom (prevents over-investment in unused docs), practical (clear documentation design guidance).
