### NEW (2026-08-26 cycle 7): Affective Paternalism Cudge Framework (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/affective-paternalism-cudge-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the Affective Paternalism (AP) framework that positions affect as a primary policy resource rather than a bias to be corrected (Västfjäll, Asutay & Tinghög, Linköping University, Frontiers in Behavioral Economics, June 2026). The "cudge" (cue + nudge) modifies the affective architecture of choices rather than their cognitive structure. CARE taxonomy: Create (build new integral affective associations), Attenuate (reduce disproportionate intensity), Reinforce (amplify and redirect existing positive affect), Eliminate (disrupt miscalibrated responses). Integral vs incidental affect distinction: integral (genuinely about the decision) outperforms incidental (normatively unrelated). Evidence: N=1,085,322 organ donation trial (reciprocity message +38%, smiling photos reduced effectiveness); donation bundling 76% increase in effective giving with $1.5M+ raised; satisfies asymmetric paternalism criterion. A-Tech alignment: open-source (theoretical framework), data privacy (behavioral proxies), financial freedom (welfare-superior at negligible cost), practical implementation (four-mode taxonomy with diagnostic rules).

### NEW (2026-08-26 cycle 7): FedGSA Grassmann Manifold DP Federated LoRA (`privacy-and-trust/fedgsa-grassmann-manifold-dp-federated-lora/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first geometry-consistent aggregation framework for differentially private federated LoRA using the Grassmann manifold (Zheng et al., arXiv:2608.03267, 2026). Solves three challenges: aggregation mismatch, quadratic noise amplification, and basis ambiguity (BA = (BQ)(Q⁻¹A) for any invertible Q). Represents each privatized client update as a subspace point on Gr(r, d_out), aggregates projection matrices geometrically, reconstructs global LoRA factors within consensus subspace. Single-factor DP-SGD (freeze A, update B) eliminates multiplicative cross-noise. All server-side operations are post-processing → no additional privacy loss. Results: +2.17% (ε=6) and +2.27% (ε=3) over strongest baseline (FedSVD) on GLUE; first across all five tasks; heterogeneity advantage grows to +11.82% at severe non-IID. A-Tech alignment: open-source (reproducible, PyTorch), data privacy (formal (ε,δ)-DP, no trusted server), financial freedom (enables small organizations), practical (RoBERTa-base, GPT-2).

### NEW (2026-08-26 cycle 7): VeriDP Verifiable DP-SGD (`privacy-and-trust/veridp-verifiable-dp-sgd/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first framework for per-iteration verifiable differentially private training using zero-knowledge proofs (Abdolmaleki et al., Sheffield/Cambridge/Waterloo/Barkhausen Institut, PoPETs 2026(3)). Combines ZKPs with polynomial commitments, sumcheck/GKR proofs, and incrementally verifiable computation (IVC). ZK-DPSGD definition: completeness, knowledge soundness, zero-knowledge, privacy enforcement. Per-iteration proof covering seed correctness, dataset membership (Merkle), gradient computation, clipping, averaging, verifiable Gaussian noise (Box-Muller circuit), weight update, recursive IVC chaining. Anti-seed-grinding via commit-then-derive with context binding. Constant-size proofs (3-4 KB) and constant-time verification (2-5ms) regardless of training length or model size. Federated learning: each client generates ZKP, aggregator verifies BEFORE incorporating update. A-Tech alignment: open-source (github.com/BarkhausenInstitut/VeriDP, C++ ~5000 LOC), data privacy (ZK reveals nothing), financial freedom (small orgs prove compliance), practical (MLP, CNN, ResNet18).

Perceived ad effectiveness shares α clustering coefficient correlate — consistent with Narrative Transportation Theory. Distinguishes mentalizing from empathy, Theory of Mind, and perspective-taking. EEG recommended over fMRI (temporal resolution), eye-tracking (cannot access social cognition), and autonomic measures (cannot isolate inferential processes). Ethical concerns: psychological privacy, manipulation risk. A-Tech alignment: open-source (EEGLab, Brain Connectivity Toolbox), data privacy (on-device processing), practical implementation (concrete EEG correlates and protocols).

### NEW (2026-08-18): Agentic Coding Production Characterization (`developer-experience-and-flow/agentic-coding-production-characterization/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first production-scale characterization of AI coding-agent workloads (GitHub Copilot, 3.2M users, 13M sessions, 761M LLM calls, 95T tokens, June 2026). Seven structural properties: (1) 1:1 LLM↔Tool coupling — 87% agent-initiated calls, near 1:1 ratio; serving systems must treat LLM calls and tool invocations as inter-dependent pairs. (2) Session-structured KV cache — 90% hit within turns, 55% at turn boundaries, 8% after model switches; cache is session-aware schedulable resource. (3) Model switches destroy cache — 6.4% of sessions, predominantly reactive to rate limiting; -67% cache hit drop. (4) Context compaction costly — 7.8% of sessions, 44% of tokens, drops 72.8% of prompt tokens, -66.1% cache hit rate, median 22% of turn execution time. (5) Turn boundaries signal idle — median 4.1 min container / 2.9 min KV cache cross-turn; natural reclamation trigger. (6) Tool failures amplify compute — 9% of turns trigger retry loops with 4× compute amplification. (7) Heterogeneous users — 5 archetypes with 50× token range (Chat-only 23K to Deep-loop 1.1M); uniform policies suboptimal. Five user archetypes: Readers (41.7%), Coders (30.4%), Terminal users (11%), Deep-loop users (9.2%), Chat-only (7.6%). Six workflow archetypes: Deep-loop read (30.5%), LLM-only (20.2%), Multi-cycle edit (19%), Multi-cycle other (13.2%), Deep-loop w/failures (9.1%), Deep-loop run (8.1%). Idle-time predictor: LightGBM survival-curve model (2MB), ROC-AUC 0.73 for >60s idle, captures 86-90% of total idle time. A-Tech alignment: open-source (Aider, Cline, OpenHands), data privacy (internal telemetry), financial freedom (86-90% idle capture → cost savings), practical implementation (13.5M sessions).

### NEW (2026-08-18): Personalized Coding Agent Skills (`developer-experience-and-flow/personalized-coding-agent-skills/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies empirical evidence on personalized vs generic coding-agent skills. Based on Huang, Du & Lan (UMass Amherst/OpenRefinery.ai, arXiv:2608.10319, August 2026). 206 real-world sessions, 13 developers, 5 random seeds, reproducible replay framework. Counterintuitive finding: personalized skills provide only limited and inconsistent improvements (+0.97, p=.399, not significant); generic skills pooled across developers consistently outperform (+3.78, 50.95% win rate). Threshold effect: personalized skills become effective only with ≥6 relevant historical sessions (+10.17 vs baseline, +5.67 vs generic). Two-stage skill generation: bootstrap (pattern analysis template) + evidence-grounded refinement (verify each rule against ≥2 independent user turns). Replay evaluation with LLM developer simulator (89.47% semantic consistency with real developers). Skills change behavior: more extensive execution and systematic validation (test command groups 0.56→0.97, successful validation 43.1%→58.9%), not less interaction. Generic skills: more rules (25 vs 14.15 avg), more commit rules (16% vs 7.6%). Strategic recommendation: default to generic unless ≥6 relevant sessions per developer. ### NEW (2026-08-18): LLM Personalized Ads: Reality Check (`marketing-and-content/llm-personalized-ads-reality-check/`)

Key findings: (1) No significant engagement improvement — personalized messages did not outperform non-personalized; some strategies reduced engagement for certain demographics. (2) Survey-behavior gap — survey-based appeal ratings diverged from behavioral outcomes; users rate personalized ads as more appealing but don't click more. (3) Algorithmic delivery shift ≤8% — LLM cues shift delivery toward intended audience without explicit targeting, but bounded by platform's relevance predictions. Three-dimensional evaluation framework: user engagement (live testing), perceived appeal (surveys), platform behavior (algorithmic delivery analysis). Contrast with non-ad persuasion: semantic anchoring works for directly-delivered persuasion (Xu, Zhou & Zhao, Frontiers in Psychiatry Jan 2026; 16/18 conditions significant with anchoring, N=618) but ad platforms add algorithmic mediation layer. Practical recommendations: don't extrapolate from lab studies, measure behavior not just perception, expect modest algorithmic effects, test per demographic. A-Tech alignment: open-source (any LLM including LLaMA 3.1), data privacy (real platform data), financial freedom (prevents overinvestment in ineffective personalization), practical implementation (real Meta deployment, behavioral metrics).

Changes in DevEx did NOT correlate with changes in productivity (all p>0.313). ### NEW (2026-08-04): MCP Stateless Core 2026 (`ai-agents-and-workflows/mcp-stateless-core-2026/`)

Three new official extensions: MCP Apps (server-rendered interactive UIs in AI clients), MCP Tasks (long-running async tasks with durable handles), Enterprise Managed Authorization (corporate IdP as gatekeeper). Scale metrics: 250M weekly SDK downloads, 240 AAIF members (fastest-growing Linux Foundation project), 17K+ public servers. Security: closes OAuth mix-up attacks, client credentials bound to issuer. Deprecations: Roots, Sampling, Logging, legacy HTTP+SSE transport. ### NEW (2026-08-04): KNEXA-FL Peer LLM Federation (`privacy-and-trust/knexa-fl-peer-llm-federation/`)

Key innovation: a non-aggregating Central Profiler/Matchmaker (CPM) that formulates P2P collaboration as a contextual bandit problem using LinUCB on abstract agent profiles. The CPM never accesses models — it only learns optimal matchmaking policy from reward signals. Actual knowledge transfer occurs directly between matched peers via secure text-based distillation. Results on heterogeneous code generation (6 agents, 410M-620M parameters, Dirichlet non-IID): +50% relative improvement in Pass@1 over random P2P collaboration; stable convergence (vs catastrophic performance collapse in centralized distillation baselines); sub-linear regret of LinUCB matchmaker relative to oracle pairing. Architecture: privacy-preserving agent profiles (sanitized data/task summaries), LinUCB contextual bandit for peer selection, adaptive knowledge distillation (soft targets via temperature scaling), guardrail filters for safety. This is the first framework to show that intelligent matchmaking can make P2P LLM federation practical — combining the privacy benefits of decentralization with the efficiency of centralized approaches. ### NEW (2026-08-14): ERIS Federated Shard Aggregation (`privacy-and-trust/eris-federated-shard-aggregation/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the ERIS framework for privacy-preserving federated learning that achieves FedAvg-equivalent utility, information-theoretic privacy amplification (leakage bounded by n*T*p/A*C_max), and scalable distributed aggregation without heavy cryptography or utility-degrading perturbations. Based on Fenoglio et al. (arXiv:2602.08617v2, May 2026). Key innovation: Federated Shard Aggregation (FSA) partitions each client update into A disjoint shards sent to different aggregators; because masks are disjoint and complete, reassembly produces the exact centralized update. Optional Distributed Shifted Compression (DSC) reduces transmitted and exposed coordinates. Information-theoretic privacy bound: I(D_k; observations) ≤ n*T*p/A*C_max, with FSA providing 1/A amplification and DSC providing 1/p reduction. Collusion extension: I ≤ n*T*p*A_c/A*C_max. Convergence: Õ(√(1+ω)/(m√K)) — dimension-free, no term growing with T. Empirical: matches non-private FedAvg utility (34.84% vs 34.86% on CIFAR-10) while reducing MIA accuracy (63.02% vs 68.46%); 105× communication speedup with A=50; robust to 70% dropout and 50% link failures; effective against DLG/iDLG/ROG/GGL attacks. A-Tech applications for A-Coder (federated code intelligence with adaptive privacy), Be Practical (ERIS curriculum), Builder's Club (open-source benchmark). Cross-references 4 existing privacy/FL skills. A-Tech alignment: open-source (MIT, PyTorch, Flower), data privacy (information-theoretic, no TEE/HE, data local), financial freedom (no specialized hardware, 105× communication reduction), practical implementation (Docker, reproducible 5-fold CV, robust to failure).

### NEW (2026-08-04): MCP Stateless Core 2026 (`ai-agents-and-workflows/mcp-stateless-core-2026/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification's stateless protocol core for enterprise-scale agent infrastructure. The spec removes session state from the protocol layer: no `initialize`/`initialized` handshake, no `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Every request is self-describing with protocol version, client identity, and capabilities in `_meta`. Any request can land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer. Key changes: (1) No handshake/sessions — `server/discover` RPC replaces mandatory handshake, optional discovery call for capability learning. (2) Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR) — replaces server-initiated `elicitation/create`, `sampling/createMessage`, `roots/list` that required held-open streams; server returns `resultType: "input_required"` with requests, client retries with `inputResponses`. (3) Header-based routing — `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` HTTP headers enable gateway routing/authorization without JSON body parsing. (4) Cacheable list results — `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list` responses carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`. (5) Authorization hardening — RFC 9207 issuer validation, shift from DCR to Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), client credentials bound to issuer. (6) Tasks extension — `tasks/get` and `tasks/update` with poll-based notifications via `subscriptions/listen`. (7) 12-month deprecation policy — Roots, Sampling, Logging deprecated; legacy HTTP+SSE transport deprecated. SDKs: TypeScript, Python, Go, C#, Rust (beta) all updated. Adoption: 250M weekly SDK downloads, 10K+ active servers, 240 AAIF members (fastest-growing Linux Foundation foundation). A-Tech applications for A-Coder (stateless MCP server patterns, MRTR for interactive workflows), Be Practical (MCP 2026 spec curriculum), Builder's Club (open-source stateless MCP server templates). Cross-references 4 existing MCP/agent skills. A-Tech alignment: open-source (Linux Foundation governance, multi-vendor), data privacy (stateless = no session data at risk, auth hardening), financial freedom (standard load balancers replace sticky routing, reduces infrastructure cost), practical implementation (SDKs updated, migration guides available).

### NEW (2026-08-04): KNEXA-FL Peer LLM Federation (`privacy-and-trust/knexa-fl-peer-llm-federation/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Implements orchestrated-decentralized peer-to-peer LLM federation using contextual bandit matchmaking. Based on Singh, Vissol-Gaudin, Otung & Sekiya (AAAI 2026, Fujitsu Research). KNEXA-FL resolves the trade-off between centralized aggregation (security vulnerability — single point of attack) and random P2P pairing (statistical inefficiency). The Central Profiler/Matchmaker (CPM) uses a LinUCB contextual bandit algorithm on abstract agent profiles to learn optimal peer-matching policy — without accessing any model weights or data. Knowledge transfer occurs directly between matched peers via secure text-based distillation. Key results: +50% relative improvement in Pass@1 over random P2P collaboration on heterogeneous code generation (6 agents, 410M-620M parameters); stable convergence vs. centralized distillation baselines that suffer catastrophic collapse; sub-linear LinUCB regret vs. oracle pairing. Architecture: non-aggregating CPM (never touches models), privacy-preserving agent profiles, adaptive knowledge distillation between peers, guardrail filters with SIER (Safety-Integrity-Ethics-Robustness), gRPC P2P communication. Heterogeneous backbone support (Qwen-0.5B, Cerebras-GPT-590M, BLOOM-560M, Pythia-410M). A-Tech applications for A-Coder (federated code intelligence without central server), Be Practical (P2P FL curriculum), Builder's Club (open-source KNEXA-FL toolkit). Cross-references 4 existing federated learning skills. A-Tech alignment: open-source (BSD-3-Clause, PyTorch, Flower, reproducible artifacts), data privacy (non-aggregating CPM, profiles are abstracted/sanitized, knowledge transfer via distillation not raw data), financial freedom (no central server infrastructure cost, works on commodity GPUs), practical implementation (AAAI-validated, CPU-only artifact reproduction, 6-agent config).

### NEW (2026-08-16): Mecha-Nudges for Machines (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/mecha-nudges-for-machines/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Designs choice architecture interventions that systematically influence AI agents (LLM shopping/recommendation agents) without degrading the human decision environment. Based on Frey & Ethayarajh, University of Chicago (arXiv:2603.23433, 2026). Introduces the concept of mecha-nudges: changes to how choices are presented that systematically influence AI agents without degrading the human environment. Distinguishes mecha-nudges from prompt injection (preserve options, act on environment) and traditional SEO (SEO targets machines as presentation layer for humans; mecha-nudges target machines as decision-makers). Formal framework: Bayesian persuasion + V-usable information (observer-relative generalization of Shannon information). The mecha-nudging design problem: maximize machine-usable information while not decreasing human-usable information beyond tolerance ε. Empirical evidence: Etsy natural experiment (~6M listings, 1.06M pre-ChatGPT, ~5M post) shows +0.143 bits machine-usable information increase; robust across prompts and models (GPT-5-mini, Gemma-3-27B, Qwen3-32B); absent in art/collectibles (humans are AI-sensitive), stronger in consumer staples. Three robustness checks: placebo rephrasing (effect is semantic not syntactic), DailyMed control (no comparable increase in non-agent-mediated text), category interactions (economically rational variation). Token-level patterns: scarcity words (prolific, scarce, oddities) increase machine predictability; affective words (cheery, radiance, sincere) decrease it. Practical framework for A-Tech: how open-source AI projects can optimize for agent discoverability (structured attributes over prose, scarcity/availability signals over affective language, machine-readable metadata, cross-model testing, ε-constrained human readability). A-Tech applications for A-Coder (V-usable-information-based tool recommendation), Be Practical ("Writing for Agents" curriculum), Builder's Club (open-source mecha-nudge audit tool). Cross-references 6 existing skills. A-Tech alignment: open-source (V-usable info is observer-relative, open-weight models enable auditing), data privacy (acts on public text, no surveillance), financial freedom (merit-based agent discoverability without ad spend), practical implementation (token-level patterns immediately actionable, 6M-listing-scale empirical validation).
- **references/mecha-nudge-evidence-base.md** — Full evidence base: Etsy natural experiment design (6M listings, 1.06M pre-ChatGPT, ~5M post, V-usable information measurement methodology), headline result (+0.143 bits), three robustness checks (placebo rephrasing — semantic not syntactic; DailyMed control — no increase in non-market text; category interactions — absent in art/collectibles, stronger in consumer staples), cross-model robustness (GPT-5-mini, Gemma-3-27B, Qwen3-32B), formal mathematical framework (V-usable information definition, properties, relation to Bayesian persuasion, Proposition 1 informal statement on mecha-nudge feasibility), token ablation methodology and results table (scarcity words increase I_V, affective words decrease I_V, cross-model consistency), implications for open-source AI market design (agent discoverability, merit-based ranking, dual-usable documentation standard, adversarial mecha-nudge defense, regulatory implications), supporting literature (Kamenica & Gentzkow 2011, Shannon 1948, Thaler & Sunstein 2008, Cherep et al. 2026), six open questions, cross-references, A-Tech alignment.

### NEW (2026-08-16): VPDR Variance-Adaptive Prototype Perturbation (`privacy-and-trust/vpdr-variance-adaptive-prototype-perturbation/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Implements variance-adaptive noise allocation for privacy-preserving prototype-based personalized federated learning. Based on Wang et al. (CVPR 2026). Solves Isotropic Gaussian Prototype Perturbation (IGPP) over-perturbation of discriminative dimensions and clipping-threshold dilemma. Two modules: VPP (Variance-adaptive Prototype Perturbation) computes dimension-wise discriminative scores from intra/inter-class variance, privately selects discriminative subspace via oneshot Laplace Top-k, allocates less noise to discriminative dimensions; DCR (Distillation-guided Clipping Regularization) uses differentiable soft-clipping + EMA teacher-student knowledge distillation for prediction consistency. Privacy: (ε,δ)-LDP via sequential composition, no weaker than isotropic baseline. Results: consistent accuracy gains across 6 ProtoPFL frameworks × 3 benchmarks (Digits, Office-Caltech, PACS); largest gains under extreme label skew. Attack defense: drives MIA ROC-AUC to chance (~0.50), throttles FSH Top-1 Hit to ~20%. Overhead: only 8.1% runtime increase. Open-source: github.com/yuCoryx/ProtoPFL_VPDR. A-Tech alignment: open-source code, data privacy (LDP guarantees), practical implementation (CVPR-validated, low overhead).
- **references/vpdr-evidence-base.md** — Full evidence base: mathematical formulations (discriminative score, oneshot Laplace, groupwise clipping, noise allocation), Theorems 4.1 and 4.2, full experimental results tables, ablation study, privacy attack results table, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.

### NEW (2026-08-14): Nudge Transparency Disclosure Effectiveness (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/nudge-transparency-disclosure-effectiveness/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the disclosure transparency framework for nudging interventions, distinguishing four disclosure types and their differential effects on nudge effectiveness and perceived autonomy. Based on Cuypers, Raymaekers & Van de Walle (Behavioural Public Policy, May 2026; n=1,916 vignette experiment, Flemish representative sample). Four disclosure types following de Ridder et al. (2022): presence (behavioral techniques used), purpose (policy goal), mechanism (how it works), combined (all three). Key findings: the salience nudge was effective (+10.4pp sustainable dish selection); NO disclosure significantly changed nudge effectiveness — neither enhanced nor reduced it; the nudge itself caused a small but significant autonomy decrease (-2.4pp) that NO disclosure could offset; three of four disclosures were statistically equivalent to nudge-only on autonomy. Theoretical implications: contradicts persuasion knowledge model expectation (presence disclosure should trigger suspicion), contradicts self-determination theory expectation (purpose disclosure should enhance autonomy), no evidence of psychological reactance. Central tension: disclosures can be applied without compromising effectiveness but are not sufficient to mitigate autonomy concerns. Salience vs default nudge distinction: salience nudges are theoretically more overt than defaults, yet even they reduce autonomy slightly. Limitations: vignette methodology, single nudge type, low attention (40%+ manipulation check failure), autonomy construct heterogeneity. A-Tech applications for A-Coder (transparent nudge design), Be Practical (disclosure curriculum), Builder's Club (open-source transparency framework). Cross-references 5 existing nudging skills. A-Tech alignment: open-source (open access, preregistered, R code), data privacy (GDPR-compliant, anonymous), financial freedom (disclosures are free to implement, maintain effectiveness), practical implementation (1,916 participants, preregistered, R code, directly applicable).

### NEW (2026-07-25): Chain Federated Fine-Tuning (`privacy-and-trust/chain-federated-fine-tuning/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Enables privacy-preserving LLM adaptation on memory-constrained edge devices by training adapters sequentially (chain optimization) rather than end-to-end, breaking the memory wall that excludes low-end devices from federated learning. CHAINFED (Wu et al., ACL 2026): for LLaMA2-7B, base parameters consume 91.2% of the ~27 GB footprint; standard adapter-based federated tuning fails to scale to modern LLMs on 4–12 GB devices. Three core techniques: Dynamic Layer Co-Tuning (sliding window bridges semantic gaps and breaks gradient isolation), Globally Perceptive Optimization (auxiliary output branch balances local + global loss), Function-Oriented Adaptive Tuning (CKA similarity identifies the optimal fine-tuning starting layer; T=0.8 optimal). Outperforms both memory-aware baselines and the memory-unconstrained upper bound (LLaMA3.1-8B: +10.71% avg accuracy, 3.45× memory reduction). Sovereign-data-ecosystem properties: raw data never leaves the device; only adapter gradients are aggregated. A-Tech alignment: operates on open-weight models; runs on 8 GB RAM laptops / Raspberry Pi 4; inherently GDPR/CCPA compliant.
- **references/chainfed-evidence-base.md** — Wu et al. (ACL 2026) full results, memory-wall quantification (LLaMA2-7B/13B breakdown), performance degradation under memory constraints, ablation study (all three components indispensable), FOAT threshold sensitivity (T=0.8 optimal, up to 4.43% gain + 2.02× faster + 3.47× lower communication), co-tuning window trade-off, instruction-tuning results (LLaMA2-7B, LLaMA3.1-8B), convergence analysis, I/O latency mitigation, and related frameworks (FEDOT, FedPKDA, Apple FL, Google ODP).

- **SKILL.md** — Applies the Stimulus-Organism-Response + dual-process model from Nagpal et al. (Frontiers in Psychology, March 2026; N=609, PLS-SEM) that explains which neuromarketing stimuli drive impulsive consumer behaviour and which do not, moderated by consumer traits. The evidence-based stimulus ranking: emotional appeals (β=0.469, strongest), cognitive processing cues (β=0.378), sensory triggers (β=0.173), neuro-pricing (β=0.134) are significant; scarcity/urgency (β=0.043, p=0.095) and endorsement influence (β=0.045, p=0.127) are NOT significant in digitally saturated environments — a direct contravention of conventional marketing wisdom. Neuromarketing efficacy → impulsivity (β=0.562); consumer traits moderate the chain (β=0.075, p<0.001) — the consumers most vulnerable to impulsivity exploitation are the ones the stimuli work hardest on. Provides the trait-contingent segmentation (emotional susceptibility / FOMO / social-influence sensitivity), the four-lever prioritisation, the two-lever de-prioritisation, the ethical guardrails, and the A-Tech application matrix. Complements `neuromarketing-sor-trait-moderation-model` (predates this study) and `predictive-neuromarketing-bayesian-framework` (computational theory).

### 14. Privacy-Preserving AI Attribution Framework (`privacy-and-trust/privacy-preserving-ai-attribution-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Traces an AI agent's output back to its training data without exposing sensitive personal information. The core inversion: "protect then attribute" (privacy as foundation, attribution built on top), not "attribute then protect." The five-step stack: (1) federated learning (raw data never leaves its source — branches train local models, only parameter updates sent to central server); (2) differential privacy during aggregation (calibrated epsilon 0.5-2.0 — always err on the side of more privacy; a privacy breach is permanent but model accuracy can be recovered); (3) homomorphic encryption for targeted attribution queries (encrypt target record → cryptographic influence calculation on encrypted data → decrypt only the yes/no result); (4) explainable AI via SHAP/LIME for high-level lineage (which features were influential, without revealing individual data); (5) data governance and minimization (collect only necessary data, retention policies, automated deletion, access controls, audit trails — established *before* deploying any attribution solution). Measurable enterprise outcomes (regional bank, 18 months): 75% reduction in privacy audit findings, 20% increase in customer AI trust scores, auditable proof of non-discrimination without compromising individual data. The competitive-advantage thesis: privacy-preserving attribution is not just regulatory burden but competitive advantage. A-Tech applications: A-Coder enterprise licensing differentiator (attribution stack as premium tier for regulated industries), Be Practical curriculum module, Builder's Club open-source reference architecture. Composes with `federated-learning-for-privacy-preserving-ai` (Step 1), `differential-privacy-synthetic-data` + `sheld-fl-self-learning-heterogeneous-dp-framework` + `slaclip-adaptive-clipping-dp-sgd` (Step 2), `post-quantum-privacy-architecture` (Step 3), `algorithmic-transparency-accountability` (Step 4 complement), `eu-ai-act-developer-compliance-2026` (Step 5 compliance driver), `privacy-first-competitive-differentiator` (business case).

### 15. Agent-Friendly API Documentation 2026 (`developer-experience-and-flow/agent-friendly-api-documentation-2026/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The writing craft for API documentation that AI agents can reliably retrieve, parse, and use to take the correct action — not just documentation humans can read. The key difference: human-focused documentation optimizes for learning/exploration; agent-focused documentation optimizes for retrieval/execution, and the biggest axis is tolerance for ambiguity. Six steps: (1) use OpenAPI as the source of truth with behavior-defining descriptions (preconditions, valid transitions, recovery — not just shape); (2) document workflows, not just endpoints (explicit multi-step sequencing for common tasks); (3) keep terminology consistent (one canonical term per concept; agents treat synonyms as separate concepts); (4) write descriptions that work for LLMs (intent + preconditions + boundaries, not just function — the `description` field is execution surface); (5) add `llms.txt` as a discovery/prioritization layer (points agents to canonical docs; not a replacement for OpenAPI; respect the paid-tier boundary from `ai-license-circumvention-defense`); (6) serve Markdown and raw specs where possible (visual docs for humans; parseable formats for agents). The seven questions every endpoint must answer. The 12-item agent-ready documentation checklist. Platform examples: Cash App (`/llms.txt` + `/llms-full.txt`), Stripe (MCP server), Rightbrain, Fern, n8n. Core principle: documentation is becoming part of the agent runtime — it shapes how automated systems discover tools, choose actions, and recover from errors. ### 16. Predictive Neuromarketing Bayesian Framework (`marketing-and-content/predictive-neuromarketing-bayesian-framework/`)

Four key mechanisms: price placebo (price cue as high-precision prior on quality), brand-identity modulation (brand cue as high-precision prior at semantic level; reinterprets McClure Coke-vs-Pepsi), EEG-based preference prediction (spectral features as correlates of prediction error at specific hierarchy levels; >90% accuracy decodes posterior over value), neuroforecasting (subcortical affective prediction error generalises to aggregate market behaviour; explains say-do gap). A-Tech applications: A-Coder (cognitive load as prediction-error precision), Be Practical (learning as prediction-error minimisation), Builder's Club (community engagement as social prediction-error minimisation), A-Tech neuromarketing ethics (auditable forward-prediction structure). ### 17. Optimal Nudging Resource-Rational Framework (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/optimal-nudging-resource-rational-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — A computational framework for modeling, predicting, and automatically constructing optimal nudges by treating nudges as modifications to the meta-level problem a resource-rational agent faces (the problem of how to decide, not what to decide). Uses meta-level Markov decision processes (meta-level MDPs): nudges change the cost of computations or the agent's initial beliefs, changing the optimal sequence of cognitive operations, which changes the belief at choice time and the choice itself. Three canonical nudge types mapped to meta-level modifications: defaults (change initial belief — agent treats default as recommendation), suggestions (add option + reveal best feature), information highlighting (reduce cost of considering certain features). Meta-greedy policy produces quantitative predictions without free parameters. Five-step optimal-nudge construction method (model decision → specify nudge space → specify objective → specify architect's belief → optimize). Digital nudging architecture: three sequential processing layers (Data Capture → User Modeling → Nudge Intelligence) + two cross-cutting evaluation modules (Adaptation + Evaluation with Fairness Monitor, Ethics Compliance, Explainability, Outcome Tracker). 11 quality attributes. Validated in five experiments (N=400/272/88/250/250): defaults increase selection (89.8% vs 55.7%), early suggestions outperform late, highlighting shifts consideration, optimal nudges outperform random and heuristic. A-Tech applications: A-Coder (AI suggestions as information-highlighting nudges), Be Practical (learning modules as choice architecture), Builder's Club (community feed optimization for engagement quality not quantity), privacy-first personalization (operate without user data by integrating over all possible preferences). Complements `bottom-nudge-analysis-framework` (mechanism typology), `digital-nudging-ethical-persuasion`, `ai-behavioral-loop-design`, `nudge-disclosure-transparency-effectiveness`, `hyper-nudging-ai-personalization-ethics`.

### 18. Separable Expert Architecture: Deletable Personalization (`privacy-and-trust/separable-expert-architecture-deletable-personalization/`)
- **SKILL.md** — A three-layer LLM personalization architecture that decouples user-specific data from shared model weights by combining a frozen base model, shared domain-expert LoRA adapters, and a per-user proxy artifact (routing bias + contrastive steering vectors + personal LoRA, ~2–5 MB) whose filesystem deletion constitutes deterministic, verified unlearning — no retraining required. The architectural invariant (Separation): all user-specific information resides in an isolated, deletable proxy; shared components contain no user-identifying information; removing the proxy is necessary and sufficient for complete user data removal. Structural, not statistical — prevents entanglement by construction rather than attempting surgical undo after the fact. Five-stage inference pipeline (Route → Bias → Merge → Steer → Generate). Three-step deletion protocol (Verify via KL divergence against cached baseline → Delete via secure filesystem removal → Audit log). Validated on Phi-3.5-mini and Llama-3.1-8B: personalization present (weight shift 0.052–0.088, Jaccard 0.236–0.316), deletion verified (82–89% pass rate, KL ~0.21 nats, bimodal distribution), cross-user isolation (contamination <=0.05). Converts machine unlearning from intractable weight-editing to deterministic deletion. Compatible with DP-SGD for shared model improvement. A-Tech applications: A-Coder (per-developer proxy, deleting developer = deleting proxy), Be Practical (learner progress in deletable proxy, shared pedagogy model stays clean), Builder's Club (member assistants with fully deletable personalization), privacy-first competitive differentiator (Right to Erasure as structural guarantee, shared model open-sourceable/auditable without user-data exposure). Complements `opal-private-memory-architecture` (memory layer), `privacy-preserving-ai-attribution-framework` (attribution layer), `ai-agent-memory-architecture` (infrastructure memory), `federated-llm-on-device-personalization` (federated alternative).
- **references/separable-expert-evidence-base.md** — Schneider, Schoenegger & Bariach (Microsoft AI, arXiv:2604.21571, 2026), the fundamental tension (personalization vs deletion), the architectural invariant, three-layer composition specification, five-stage inference pipeline, three-step deletion protocol, experimental setup (Phi-3.5-mini/Llama-3.1-8B, 4 experts, 4 user profiles), Claim 1/2/3 results, threshold sensitivity, limitations, DP-SGD extension, and grep-confirmation of novelty.

## NEW SKILLS — July 9, 2026 Research Cycle

### 23. AI Agent FinOps: Cost Optimization as Core Architecture (`monetization-and-revenue/ai-agent-finfops-cost-optimization/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Brings FinOps discipline to AI agent fleets. Six pillars: heterogeneous model routing (frontier for orchestration, mid-tier for standard, SLM for high-frequency), the Plan-and-Execute pattern (90% cost reduction: frontier plans, SLM executes, frontier verifies), strategic caching (semantic, tool-result, plan, static-context), batching and structured-output token reduction (30–60% savings), spend governance (per-agent limits, anomaly detection, approval gates), and the agent cost dashboard. Covers CLI vs. MCP token economics (200 vs 32,000–82,000 tokens — 160–410x difference). Includes the Agent FinOps Maturity Model (Instrument → Route → Optimize → Govern) and A-Tech application matrix. NVIDIA data: 7B SLM is 10–30x cheaper than 70–175B LLM. Microsoft Phi-4: 88.0% MMLU at 92% less energy. Revenera: 70% of AI producers say delivery costs undermine profitability. Directly addresses the cloud-spend profitability crisis through local-first architecture.
- **references/plan-and-execute-patterns.md** — Implementation templates for Plan-and-Execute, semantic caching, structured output token reduction, per-agent spend guard, and Claude Code token efficiency techniques (77–91% combined cost reduction).

### 24. AI Pricing Model Taxonomy 2026 (`monetization-and-revenue/ai-pricing-model-taxonomy-2026/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The Metronome AI Pricing Model Index (50+ companies cataloged) translated into a practical pricing architecture taxonomy. Seven findings: hybrid as the norm (single-track models are the minority), three credit-model functions (compute proxy, abstracted value bundle, access gating), the consumer/API pricing split (dual-track architecture as design pattern), the gate shift (features/seats → consumption/speed/model access), enterprise pricing opacity and market bifurcation, pricing velocity as competitive advantage (Cursor: 4 restructurings in <2 years), and pricing transparency as trust mechanism. Includes the four-step pricing architecture decision framework (choose tracks, credit model, tier gates, pricing velocity) and A-Tech application matrix. Updates `software-monetization-2026-outlook`, `hybrid-ai-pricing-architecture`, and `bessemer-ai-pricing-playbook-2026` with the empirical taxonomy from cataloging 50+ actual pricing models.

### 25. Recursive Language Models (`ai-agents-and-workflows/recursive-language-models/`)
- **SKILL.md** — MIT's RLM-Qwen3-8B breakthrough applied to break context window limits without context rot. RLMs treat long prompts as external environments the model can programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over — enabling processing two orders of magnitude beyond context windows. Covers the recursive decomposition pattern (Plan → Execute → Synthesize with active navigation), context navigation vs. context dumping (active vs. passive), the RLM-Qwen3-8B performance data (+28.3% over base, approaches GPT-5 on 3 tasks at 50x smaller), three practical agent patterns (codebase analysis, long-document reasoning, multi-stage problem solver), the privacy-first local-cloud hybrid advantage (90%+ of processing stays local), and the RLM vs. conventional model decision matrix. Architecturally solves the four context failures from `context-engineering` (poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash, lost-in-the-middle).
- **references/rlm-architecture-patterns.md** — Implementation templates for basic recursive processor, codebase analysis RLM, long-document reasoning RLM, and privacy-first local-cloud hybrid RLM with code examples and cost comparison tables.

## NEW SKILLS — July 11, 2026 Research Cycle

### 586. Botsitting-Botshitting Cycle (`developer-experience-and-flow/botsitting-botshitting-cycle/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Detect, measure, and break the botsitting-botshitting cycle — the hidden human labor of making AI usable (botsitting: 6.4 hrs/week, 37% of AI interaction time) and the dangerous practice of shipping unverified AI output (botshitting: 69% admit it). Based on the Glean Work AI Index 2026 (6,000 workers, US/UK/AU). Covers the botsitting taxonomy (feeding context, supervising outputs, debugging, cleanup), the three trust traps (capability/automation complacency, helpfulness/sycophancy, humanness), the three paradoxes (productivity/coordination neglect, judgment/disfluency cue erosion, ownership/AI-as-badge-of-competence), the six-step botsitting-botshitting feedback loop, the AI toggle tax (only 0.5% of Claude users use Claude alone), constructive deviance (54% of high achievers use unapproved tools), and the human infrastructure model at three levels (individual: protect the core/botsit more/reinvest dividend; team: treat AI as teammate with human accountability/peer-to-peer adoption/managers delegate coordination; organizational: measure what matters/living governance/start with work/context-rich/invest in people). Only 13% of organizations are transformative. Full A-Tech application matrix for A-Coder (context-rich default, one-tool consolidation, comprehension checkpoints), Be Practical (curriculum including "when not to use AI"), and Builder's Club (peer-to-peer learning, scars-not-wounds storytelling, two-way data visibility).
- **references/work-ai-index-2026-evidence-base.md** — Full evidence extraction: study design (6,000 workers, 3 countries, Dec 2025–Jan 2026), all headline statistics, botsitting breakdown table, botshitting by usage intensity, three botshitting forms, demographics, three paradoxes with data, tool sprawl, high AI achievers comparison table, team-level findings, organizational transformative 13% practices table, regional differences (US/UK/AU), function-level highlights, industry highlights, forward-deployed engineer growth (800%), notable quotes.

### 587. AI Productivity Measurement Gap 2026 (`developer-experience-and-flow/ai-productivity-measurement-gap-2026/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Bridge the growing visibility gap between AI-driven productivity gains and the measurement frameworks used to track them. Based on the Harness State of Engineering Excellence 2026 report (700 engineering practitioners and managers, 5 countries, April 2026). Covers the AI productivity paradox (89% say productivity improved, but 31% of developer time is invisible work), the metrics-that-don't-match-the-work problem (89% trust their metrics, 94% say key factors missing, only 6% believe frameworks can fix it), the developer trust gap (54% fear individual performance evaluation, 55% want separation of improvement data from evaluation, 4× manager-practitioner perception gap), the new unit of work (code quality, validation time, cognitive load, burnout), the three recommendations (measure the new unit, separate AI from human metrics, separate improvement from evaluation), measurement framework extending DORA/SPACE/DX Core 4 with AI-specific dimensions, and the maturity model (Blind → Aware → Measuring → Adaptive). Full A-Tech application matrix.

### 588. Untrainable-Corner Pricing Moat (`monetization-and-revenue/untrainable-corner-pricing-moat/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Build durable pricing power in the AI economy by competing in the "untrainable corner" — territory where a smarter model is irrelevant because the bottleneck is permission, trust, and institutional integration, not intelligence. Based on Sarah Guo's (Conviction) framework and MIT data (100,000+ developers): AI agents boosted code volume ~180% but shipped code rose only ~30%. Covers the verification-cost asymmetry (cheaply verifiable work becomes commodity; expensively verifiable work retains pricing power), the token economics of the moat (generic query ~$0; private-data reasoning substantially more), outcome-based pricing as moat encoded (Sierra AI: charge only on full resolution; Cognition/Devin: performance guarantee; Harvey AI: published own legal benchmark), the two-question untrainable-corner filter, and the foundation-lab-can't-win argument (the moat is permission/trust/integration, not the model). Full A-Tech application matrix.

### 30. Neuromarketing S-O-R Trait Moderation Model (`marketing-and-content/neuromarketing-sor-trait-moderation-model/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Nagpal et al.'s (2026) validated PLS-SEM structural model (N=609, Frontiers in Psychology) integrating S-O-R framework, dual-process theory, and consumer-trait moderation. Six neuromarketing determinants tested: emotional appeals (β=0.469, strongest), cognitive processing (β=0.378), sensory triggers (β=0.173), neuro-pricing (β=0.134) all significant; scarcity/urgency (β=0.043, NS) and endorsement (β=0.045, NS) insignificant in digitally saturated environments. Efficacy→impulsivity β=0.562. Consumer traits moderate the efficacy→impulsivity link (β=0.075, p<0.001) — neuromarketing is trait-contingent. R²=0.708 (impulsivity), 0.697 (efficacy). Includes stimulus investment prioritisation, privacy-preserving trait-informed segmentation, ethical guardrails (susceptible users disproportionately affected), and A-Tech application for A-Coder marketing, Be Practical content, and Builder's Club.

- **SKILL.md** — Yazdinejad & Fitz-Gerald's (University of Regina / Balsillie School of International Affairs, April 2026, The Conversation) analysis revealing that federated unlearning — the process enabling the "right to be forgotten" in federated learning systems — introduces a new cybersecurity blind spot. An attacker can inject backdoors, then request data removal; if unlearning is imperfect (as many approximation methods are), visible attack traces disappear while hidden effects remain. The security complement to the existing federated learning skill cluster.

## Cross-Skill Connections (July 5, 2026)

The four new skills form a coherent narrative across A-Tech's research domains:

1. **The Nudging Reckoning** provides the behavioral science paradigm — boosting over nudging, competence over compliance.
2. **AI as Engineering Culture Amplifier** applies this to developer organizations — AI amplifies culture, so build a strong culture (boosting at the organizational level) before scaling AI.
3. **Machine-Mediated Market Strategy** applies this to marketing — when the evaluator is a machine, build irreplaceable utility (boosting for the market) rather than manipulative persuasion (nudging the machine).
4. **Agent Protocol Stack 2026** provides the infrastructure — the six protocols that make agent-to-agent, agent-to-tool, and agent-to-interface communication standardized and interoperable.

The common thread: **build durable, autonomous, interoperable systems (boosting/culture/irreplaceable utility/protocol standards) rather than fragile, manipulated, opaque ones (nudging/dysfunction-amplification/sameness/bespoke-integration).**

### 57. Open-Source AI Structural Overdetermination (`monetization-and-revenue/open-source-ai-structural-overdetermination/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The structural economic case for why open-source AI is overdetermined — it will propagate regardless of what closed labs do, driven by three compounding forces operating simultaneously. Force 1: Layer-defense (commoditize your complement — Intel/motherboards 1995, Google/Android 2007, Meta/Llama 2023, Nvidia/$26bn; Meta walked back but ecosystem absorbed the loss). Force 2: Bazaar production economics (five Chinese labs + Mistral run parallel portfolios with different constraints; DeepSeek's compute constraints produced MoE/FP8/novel attention now industry standard; Linus' Law at frontier scale: distributed portfolio variance covers more architecture space). Force 3: Consumption economics (substitution gradient: closed frontier → hosted open at 1/10 cost → local at zero; Cambrian explosion of small vertical apps that can't afford closed rates; net new volume not stolen). The bifurcation outcome (open captures volume by token count, closed retains premium segment). Where value relocates (orchestration, inference infra, vertical apps, managed services). The operational-burden-absorbing layer (Linux won because Red Hat existed; open weights win because Cline/OpenRouter/LiteLLM exist). Four cognitive failures that cause the pattern to be missed. The geopolitical dimension. Full A-Tech application matrix.
- **references/kevin-gee-structural-case-extraction.md** — Full extraction of Kevin Gee's memo: bazaar production theory, open source vs. open standards, Linus' Law at frontier scale, five conditions for bazaar to win, historical layer-defense examples, Meta walkback analysis, Paik's substitution gradient, on-device threshold, market expansion thesis, the four cognitive failures, geopolitical consequences.

### 58. Mental Model Erosion Defense (`developer-experience-and-flow/mental-model-erosion-defense/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Prevent the erosion of developer mental models and system understanding when using AI coding assistants. Full A-Tech application matrix for A-Coder (context-rich default, explanation mode, teaching questions, manual mode, erosion detection dashboard, rotation reminders, pre-merge explanation gate), Be Practical (curriculum, exercises, assessment), and Builder's Club (community standard, mentorship matching, open-source toolkit, governance template). ### 66. Neuromarketing Three-Layer Discipline (`marketing-and-content/neuromarketing-three-layer-discipline/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Thomas Z. Ramsøy's framework (February 2026) distinguishing the three fundamentally different activities conflated under "neuromarketing": consumer neuroscience (basic research — scientific discovery, fMRI/EEG, universal mechanisms, slow timeline), translational research (neuroscience-informed marketing — converting findings into design principles, strategic frameworks, guidelines not guarantees), and applied neuromarketing (commercial application — EEG/eye-tracking/AI prediction for specific stimuli, context-specific predictions). Covers why conflation undermines credibility (expecting applied research to produce universal laws; expecting basic research to evaluate your logo), the reinforcement cycle (basic → translational → applied → feedback), the decision framework (which layer you need based on what question you're asking), AI's role across all three layers (accelerating each without collapsing them), the maturity context (rigor improved, ethics strengthened, conceptual clarity lags), ethical guardrails per layer, and vendor claim evaluation. The conceptual architecture that organizes the existing 15+ neuromarketing skills. Under 500 lines.

### 71. Uncertainty-Routed Cascade Architecture (`developer-experience-and-flow/uncertainty-routed-cascade-architecture/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The production-safe alternative to pre-classifier cost-optimization routing. Documents the Pareto trap: the 2026 consensus playbook (route simple to cheap, complex to capable) is structurally fragile in production. Three documented cases (SaaS support 4M MAU: 60% cost savings produced 4-5x quality loss; mid-market SaaS; regulated fintech). Three failure mechanisms: long-tail compression (classifiers see surface form; long tail hidden underneath), confident failure (cheap models fail opaquely vs. frontier models' recoverable hedging), distribution drift (classifier gradually misroutes as production evolves). The alternative: uncertainty-routed cascade — every query starts at the cheaper model; calibrated confidence determines escalation. Inverts the failure mode. Two enhancements: shadow scoring and quality-weighted routing. Three required measurement additions: per-tier quality monitoring, long-tail satisfaction sampling, routing confidence drift tracking. The key lesson: the measurement architecture matters more than the routing decision. ~3 engineer-weeks to build alongside; much harder retroactively.
- **references/pareto-trap-evidence-base.md** — Full extraction of all three production cases with metrics, the three failure mechanisms detailed, the measurement gap analysis, the cascade alternative with modeled economics, and cross-reference synthesis.

### 84. Commodity-Indexed AI Agent Pricing (`monetization-and-revenue/commodity-indexed-ai-agent-pricing/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Apply the three-term commodity-indexed pricing framework (P = Σ(αᵢ·Cᵢ) + β·V + γ) adapted from long-term LNG contracts to price autonomous AI agents sustainably. Resolves the three failure modes: per-seat collapse (one agent replaces many users), cost-plus meter-watching (limits adoption), pure outcome pricing catastrophic risk (transfers inference cost risk to providers). The multi-provider infrastructure floor (Σ) is commodity-indexed — automatically adjusts as inference prices drop (~80% in 2025-2026). The value-linked multiplier (β·V) captures value delivered. The platform constant (γ) sustains the platform. Introduces the Inference Capture Ratio (ICR = (Σ + β·V) / Total Inference Cost) as monetization health metric (healthy ≥ 1.5, critical < 1.0, extractive > 4.0). Market convergence evidence from Salesforce Agentforce (2024-2026 evolution), Microsoft 365 Copilot, Intercom Fin ($0.99/resolution), Zendesk ($1.50-$2.00/resolution). The privacy-first pricing moat: local-first architecture means near-zero infrastructure floor → 2-3x higher margin or competitive pricing advantage. Includes the quarterly pricing committee cycle, value metric selection table, A-Tech application matrix for all three products, and seven anti-patterns. The mathematical pricing foundation that existing pricing skills point toward but don't formalize. Under 500 lines.

### 85. Habit Formation Neuroscience 2026 (`behavioral-psychology-and-nudging/habit-formation-neuroscience-2026/`)

Overturns the 21-day myth with evidence: University of South Australia systematic review (2,600+ participants, 20 studies) found median habit formation takes 59-66 days (up to 335 for complex behaviors). Seven evidence-based principles: (1) complexity-matched timelines (59-335 days), (2) daily consistency (2.3x faster than irregular), (3) identity alignment (+32% adherence), (4) stress management (stress kills new habits via reduced cognitive flexibility), (5) accountability (2.8x maintenance multiplier), (6) implementation intentions (cue-behavior pre-commitment pre-loads basal ganglia), (7) friction reduction (outperforms motivation). The neuroscience mechanism: transition from prefrontal cortex (effortful) to basal ganglia/dorsolateral striatum (automatic), with dopamine migrating from reward to cue (explains why cue design > motivation design). Wendy Wood's 43% rule (nearly half of daily behavior is habitual). The seven-step habit design framework, A-Tech application matrix for A-Coder (daily coding practice), Be Practical (learning habits), and Builder's Club (contribution habits), privacy-first measurement (all on-device behavioral signals, zero surveillance), ethical guardrails, and eight anti-patterns. Complements `rapid-habit-transition-switch` (the when) with the how to engineer the switch. Under 500 lines.

## NEW SKILLS — July 23, 2026 Research Cycle

### 94. AI License Circumvention Defense (`monetization-and-revenue/ai-license-circumvention-defense/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Defends open-source revenue against AI-enabled copyleft license circumvention. AI code generation tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude) have created a practical path for companies to circumvent copyleft licensing obligations that once protected commercial open-source businesses. What was previously prohibitively expensive — rewriting a complex codebase to avoid GPL/AGPL requirements — can now be accomplished in a fraction of the time and cost. This is a different threat from hyperscaler commoditization that drove the 2018-2024 BSL/SSPL license wave: AI attacks the license itself, not the deployment model. Covers the "copyright laundering" mechanism (Jamie Tanna's term — AI ingests copyleft code, strips provenance/attribution/license, produces unencumbered output), the seven unresolved legal questions (derivative works from training, clean room defense compromise, AI-generated code copyrightability paradox, fair use for training, pending Doe v. GitHub case, API reimplementation fair use), why existing countermeasures fall short (code watermarking fragile for code, snippet detection misses functional reimplementation, API patents weakened by Google v. Oracle, novel AI-specific licenses face collective action problem), the defense framework mapping AI-resistant moats (accountability/support — Petabridge 19% growth; managed services — MongoDB Atlas; data moats/network effects — WordPress; privacy-first architecture — non-circumventable trust commitment), the Tailwind CSS cautionary tale (downloads doubled +126.5%, revenue fell 80%, 75% engineering layoffs), the A-Tech 6-layer defense stack (code: circumventable; license: partially; support: AI-resistant; operations: AI-resistant; community: AI-resistant; privacy: AI-resistant), community and institutional response (HashiCorp closing PRs, QEMU banning AI code, Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation, Perens Post-Open proposal), the privacy-first structural advantage (AI can copy code but cannot regenerate trust relationships, compliance certifications, data sovereignty guarantees, or zero-retention architectural commitments), the 3-question decision framework, and 6-metric measurement framework. The A-Tech-specific contribution: privacy-first architecture positioned as the non-circumventable moat — transforming a compliance feature into a structural competitive advantage against AI circumvention. Explains WHY the shift from code-access to risk-removal monetization (open-source-risk-removal-monetization-2026) is now structurally necessary.
- **references/legal-landscape-evidence-base.md** — Full legal landscape evidence: pre-AI hyperscaler pressure (MongoDB SSPL, Elastic/OpenSearch, HashiCorp/OpenTofu, Redis/Valkey), the copyright laundering mechanism (Meeker, Tanna, O'Brien), productivity data (Copilot 40% of code, $4.91B→$30.1B market, GitClear 4x cloning), all seven unresolved legal questions with case law (GEMA v. OpenAI, Thaler v. Perlmutter, Thomson Reuters v. ROSS, Nordstrom v. M&S, Computer Associates v. Altai, Google v. Oracle, Doe v. GitHub, U.S. Copyright Office reports), countermeasure analysis table, survival strategies (Petabridge accountability, managed services, data moats, Tailwind case), community response (HashiCorp, QEMU, Linux Foundation, Perens), systemic context (60% unpaid maintainers, $8.8T dependency, 10-foundation open letter), and A-Tech relevance mapping.

### 96. SlaClip Adaptive Clipping for DP-SGD (`privacy-and-trust/slaclip-adaptive-clipping-dp-sgd/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The ICML 2026 Spotlight paper from University of Southampton and Guangzhou University solving the hardest problem in differential privacy deep learning: adapting the gradient clipping threshold without spending additional privacy budget. SlaClip extracts a "Slack Indicator" — a noise-perturbed, binned CDF estimate of gradient norms — as a free byproduct of the clipping operation. Zero extra privacy consumption, richer information than Adap-Clip, dynamic target unclipped ratio preventing late-training threshold collapse. Covers the DP-SGD clipping threshold dilemma, Adap-Clip's two problems (extra privacy cost, fixed target ratio), SlaClip's core observation (slack is not waste information), the Slack Indicator as binned CDF, plug-and-play integration with PyTorch Opacus and TensorFlow Privacy, federated learning integration (better utility per epsilon for clients, more budget for aggregation, per-client non-IID adaptation), privacy-first on-device training stack placement, comparison table (Fixed vs Adap-Clip vs SlaClip), measurement framework, A-Tech application matrix for all three products, and seven anti-patterns.
- **references/slaclip-icml-2026-evidence-base.md** — Full paper extraction: authors and institutions, DP-SGD fundamentals, the clipping problem, Adap-Clip limitations, SlaClip's innovation (Slack Indicator as binned CDF), the two key advantages (zero extra privacy, dynamic target ratio), fair comparison experimental protocol, results, three defining properties, ecosystem relationships, A-Tech privacy-first stack integration diagram, related research, open-source code link, and citation.

- **SKILL.md** — Names and counters the empirically documented failure mode where brief AI explanations raise user reliance and trust by signaling competence (perceived ability) WITHOUT deepening understanding. The ability-cue mechanism: rationales → perceived ability → trust → reliance (NOT rationales → understanding → calibrated trust). Four boundary conditions: task difficulty dilutes the ability cue on hard tasks (but reliance is NOT moderated); domain expertise makes experts MORE susceptible (fluency heuristic); attitudinal vs. behavioral trust decouple (surveys miss it); audience specificity is the fix. The harmful-explanation paradox (Buçinca, Bansal, fluency heuristic). The calibrated-explanation design framework (5 principles: match depth to stakes/audience; disclose uncertainty; differentiate by audience; measure behavioral reliance separately; treat explanation as trust-claim not knowledge-transfer). The A-Tech-specific contribution: explains WHY the existing `trust-calibration-ux-pattern` vanity-trust-score warning happens — the ability cue is the mechanism. Cross-references 7 existing skills. Under 500 lines.
- **references/sassmannshausen-evidence-base.md** — Full study extraction: design, conditions, mediation analysis, all boundary conditions, the practitioner summary, the harmful-explanation literature connection, the fluency heuristic mechanism, and the link to the broader A-Tech trust and explanation skill cluster.

### 101. Sovereign Tech Fund Causal Impact (`monetization-and-revenue/sovereign-tech-fund-causal-impact/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The first causal-evidence framework for the impact of public funding on open-source software sustainability. Based on Burin (2026, arXiv:2607.05413, CC BY 4.0, Sovereign Tech Agency). The Generalized Synthetic Control Method with propensity-score-matched donor pools (62 control repos, 12 treated, 4 flagship projects: PyPI, curl, Fortran, RubyGems). The finding: STF funding significantly increases project velocity (commits +143.8%, merged change requests +175.5%, new change requests +137.8%, new issues +249%) but has NO significant effect on releases, contributors, or closed issues. Interpretation: funding mobilizes existing development activity but does not expand the contributor base or resolve backlog. The Goal-Question-Metric + CHAOSS measurement chain. The portfolio logic (STF for velocity; Fellowship for contributors; Resilience for critical issues). The policy implication: match metrics to program objectives; money alone doesn't resolve the maintainer-capacity constraint. The AI-noise caveat on new-issue metrics. The open-source code repository (github.com/ldmnch/thesis_mds_2026). Cross-references 6 existing skills. Under 500 lines.
- **references/stf-causal-impact-evidence-base.md** — Full extraction: STA context, study design, PSM + GSCM methodology, all ATT results with significance, four project cases, GQM + CHAOSS chain, AI-noise caveat, discussion/limitations, policy implications, relationship to A-Tech skill library, and citation.

## NEW SKILLS — July 29, 2026 Research Cycle

### 28. CLI Agentic Coding Adoption & Impact (`developer-experience-and-flow/cli-agentic-coding-adoption-impact/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Applies the first enterprise-scale telemetry study of agentic command-line coding tools (Murphy-Hill, Butler & Savelieva, Microsoft, arXiv:2607.01418, July 2026) to design rollout, adoption, and retention strategies. Studying tens of thousands of engineers over Microsoft's early-2026 rollout of Claude Code and Copilot CLI, it quantifies: (1) adoption is social — skip-level peer use drives +216% trial odds (strongest signal), direct manager use +82%, reviewer peer use +54%; (2) retention is behavioral — baseline PR activity is the strongest retention predictor (+31% at 2+ PRs/week) while prior IDE Copilot use predicts AGAINST retention (−15%); (3) adopters merged ~24% more pull requests (CausalImpact, 95% CI +14.5% to +33.7%, p<0.001) with a convex dose-response curve (+15% at 3 days/week to +50.1% at 5+ days/week); (4) the lift persists across the 4-month window (no fade, contrasting the Cursor fade-out finding); (5) what engineers DO (peer ties, PR cadence) explains adoption better than WHO they are (career stage, tenure barely matter); (6) senior ICs exploit the tools better (decompose, vet, parallelize) while juniors "don't know what they don't know." Includes the social-seeding rollout playbook, the adoption–retention divergence framework, the dose-response measurement methodology, and the token-spend ROI framework with the quality-measurement caveat. A-Tech applications for A-Coder (peer-visibility features, dose-tracking, merged-PR-lift dashboards), Be Practical (org rollout chapter), and Builder's Club (Agentic Engineering Day events, open-source dose-response methodology).
- **references/microsoft-cli-agent-study-evidence.md** — Full study methodology, statistical models (discrete-time hazard, CausalImpact BSTS, within-person Poisson FE), the tool comparison (Copilot CLI 2.2× Claude Code lift), the 609-response qualitative survey themes, the dose-response curve, persistence analysis, placebo test, threats to validity, and the token-spend context (Meta's 60 trillion tokens/30 days, $1.4M/month extreme).

### 29. AI Agent Monetization Platform Selection (`monetization-and-revenue/ai-agent-monetization-platform-selection/`)
- **SKILL.md** — An 8-platform decision framework for choosing the right monetization infrastructure for AI agent products (Nevermined, Paid.AI, Skyfire, Stripe, Orb, Alguna, Chargebee, Zuora+Togai). Organized around the fundamental agent-native vs. retrofitted architectural distinction: agent-native platforms (Nevermined, Skyfire) handle agent-to-agent payments natively with protocol support (A2A, MCP, x402) and sub-dollar micropayment economics, while retrofitted traditional billing (Stripe, Chargebee, Zuora) requires weeks of custom development and loses 63% of revenue to fees on $0.50 transactions. Covers the implementation-speed matrix (<20 min Nevermined vs. 4–8 weeks Zuora), the settlement-option matrix (crypto+fiat vs. fiat-only), the Flex Credits micropayment solution, third-party neutral metering for enterprise trust (tamper-proof append-only logs, zero-trust reconciliation), and the segment-based decision framework (solo developer → startup → enterprise). Includes the ACP (OpenAI+Stripe) and Agentic Ads (70% revenue share, MCP Market) ecosystem developments. A-Tech applications for A-Coder (Nevermined backbone, Flex Credits, tamper-proof metering), Be Practical (platform-selection chapter, agent-native vs. retrofitted distinction), and Builder's Club (Nevermined ID standardization, open-source evaluation criteria). Complements `real-time-metering-ai-agent-revenue` (metering architecture), `agentic-payments-protocol-ap2` (protocol selection), and `agent-marketplace-builder-economy` (marketplace economics).
- **references/platform-comparison-evidence.md** — Full 8-platform feature breakdown (Nevermined Pay + Nevermined ID, Paid.AI, Skyfire, Stripe+ACP, Orb, Alguna, Chargebee, Zuora+Togai), market sizing ($52.62B by 2030, 46.3% CAGR; $3–5T agentic commerce by 2030), implementation-speed and settlement-option matrices, the Valory case study (6 weeks → 6 hours), the Revenera MCP Server launch (July 2026), the Agentic Ads network, and the protocol-support comparison table.

### 30. Neuromarketing Predictive Purchase Intent Model (`marketing-and-content/neuromarketing-predictive-purchase-intent-model/`)
- **SKILL.md** — A quantitative, evidence-based model for predicting consumer purchase intent from EEG neural engagement and eye-tracking visual attention. Built on a 285-participant study (Iyappan et al., JMSR, Nov 2025) using a 32-channel Emotiv EEG and Tobii Pro Nano eye-tracker across 20 video ads spanning four product categories. The regression model (R² = 0.53) identifies the predictor hierarchy: fixation duration (β = 0.38, the most powerful predictor) > frontal alpha activity (β = 0.31, positive emotion/approach motivation) > number of fixations (β = 0.21) > frontal beta activity (β = 0.18, cognitive arousal). Emotional ads outperform informational ads (4.01 vs 3.43 purchase intent, p<0.001), and product category moderates the effect (fashion highest at 3.95, electronics lowest at 3.51). Includes the 6-step pre-launch testing protocol (recruit → stimuli → measure → analyze → optimize → deploy), the privacy-first behavioral-proxy translation framework (fixation duration → dwell time/replay rate; frontal alpha → share rate/sentiment; all on-device, no biometric collection), and the A-Tech application matrix. Distinct from `neuromarketing-consumer-journey-3x3-framework` (the stage typology), `closed-loop-cognition-marketing` (the optimization loop), and `neuro-marketing-privacy-first-behavioral-analytics` (the architecture).
- **references/purchase-intent-study-evidence.md** — Full study design (285 participants, 20 ads, 4 categories, 2 ad types), statistical tables (descriptives, correlations, regression coefficients, model summary, ANOVA), hypothesis results, key findings summary, acknowledged limitations, the privacy-first translation framework with validation thesis, and the related research context (Afshar & Azimi 2025, Vecchiato et al. 2014, Byrne et al. 2022).

### SHELD-FL Self-Learning Heterogeneous DP Framework (`privacy-and-trust/sheld-fl-self-learning-heterogeneous-dp-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — Deploys SHELD-FL (Self-learning Heterogeneous-based privacy-Enhanced end-to-end Learning Design for Federated Learning), the 2026 privacy-adaptive FL framework (Complex & Intelligent Systems, Springer Nature, DOI 10.1007/s40747-026-02266-8). Solves the core limitation of uniform-noise DP in FL: over-protects low-sensitivity gradients (wasting utility), under-protects high-sensitivity ones (risking privacy), and degrades accuracy under non-IID data. Four mechanisms: self-learning privacy budgeting (dynamic ε per round by gradient sensitivity), heterogeneous differential privacy (per-client noise by data sensitivity), client-side gradient boosting classifier (non-IID robustness), server-side Builder Optimization Algorithm (BOA) for noise regulation. Results: 98.39% accuracy at ε=10 (3-5% above baseline), ~40% communication-latency reduction, on EHRs from simulated blood-bank institutions. Deployment decision matrix (when to use SHELD-FL vs federated-byzantine-robust-partial-participation vs slaclip-adaptive-clipping-dp-sgd). Implementation notes (sensitivity tagging, non-IID robustness without the booster, BOA warm-up, composition with DMA for Byzantine robustness). A-Tech applications for A-Coder (privacy layer for federated fine-tuning in healthcare/finance verticals), Builder's Club (open-source SHELD-FL or simplified self-learning-budget variant), Be Practical (adaptive vs uniform DP principle: privacy budget follows risk, not spread evenly).
- **references/sheld-fl-study-evidence.md** — Source abstract, mechanism summary, reported results with caveats (single-domain simulated validation, paywalled full text, emerging replication), the broader 2026 adaptive-DP-FL research landscape (SlaClip, DMA, the systematic review, RDP-based privacy-adaptive works), the convergent insight (privacy budget should follow risk), and cross-references to the existing privacy-and-trust skill ecosystem.

## NEW SKILLS — July 15, 2026 Research Cycle

### Harness Maturity Matrix (`developer-experience-and-flow/harness-maturity-matrix/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The AI engineering maturity model: a 10-dimension × 5-stage diagnostic matrix for assessing and advancing a team's AI harness practices. Synthesizes the convergent "harness engineering" community insight (Hashimoto, OpenAI team, Boeckeler, Fowler, Morris) that when AI writes the code, the craft shifts to designing the system that controls AI. The five stages (No AI Process → Chatbot-Assisted → Human-in-the-Loop → Systematic Harness → Agentic Flywheel) span ten dimensions organized into four causal clusters (Foundation → Governance → Delivery → Outcomes & Learning): Context Engineering, Team (Humans + Agents), Security & Trust, Architectural Governance, Human-Agent Interaction, Workflow & Process, Reliability & Operations, Verification & Quality, Knowledge & Feedback Loops, Planning & Decision-Making. Covers the loop progression (outside → in → on → flywheel), the "probabilistic inside, deterministic at the edges" principle, "taste is the new moat" (taste invariants as code), "agents as first-class team members," the brownfield reality check (Stages 1-3 apply equally; Stage 4 largely unvalidated for debt-laden legacy), the harness-readiness checklist (modularization, boundary enforcement, test coverage), the mixed-maturity-is-the-norm finding (the weaker dimension is the bottleneck), the regression pattern, and the domain-depth nuance (agents provide technical depth, not domain depth). The organizational/maturity complement to `harness-engineering-ai-agents-2026` (the technical layers). Under 500 lines.

### Outer-Loop Harness Framework: RPI/BMAD/SPARC (`ai-agents-and-workflows/outer-loop-harness-framework/`)
- **SKILL.md** — The three production outer-loop agentic coding harnesses and the seven-dimensional framework selection model. RPI (Research-Plan-Implement): research-first interrogation preventing agents from jumping to code; best for complex multi-component and high-stakes systems. BMAD™ (Breakthrough Method for Agile AI-Driven Development): agent-as-code with hyper-detailed stories and mandatory Test Architect for brownfield; best for medium-high complexity and consistency. SPARC (Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, Completion): five-phase from-scratch methodology with strongest greenfield optimization; validated by Adrian Cockcroft (Netflix/AWS) building iOS in Swift autonomously. The seven dimensions that matter more than brownfield/greenfield (codebase size, tech stack maturity, team size, velocity requirements, cost management, security/compliance, the task half-life). The 35-minute task half-life finding (AI agents perform best on ~35-minute human-time tasks; doubling duration quadruples failure rate — exponential, not linear). The 20-35% greenfield advantage across all frameworks. The context engineering hierarchy of effort (research > planning > implementation; a single research misunderstanding = thousands of erroneous lines). The 300K-line brownfield success case (7 hours, three-phase approach, context under 40%). The framework selection guide (IDE tools vs structured methodologies vs enterprise solutions vs mandated context engineering). The vertical-deployment insight (function-specific agent squads >> horizontal enterprise-wide copilots). The <10% pilot-to-production rate. The value relocation (from framework selection to domain-specific customization). The methodology/operational complement to `harness-engineering-ai-agents-2026` (technical layers) and `harness-maturity-matrix` (organizational maturity). Under 500 lines.

855. **NEW:** OpenAffect Insights (2026) — "What is neuromarketing in 2026? (And why most of what you have read is wrong)." The direction-of-inference distinction. Legacy category (EEG-cap vendor market, reverse inference, Nielsen consolidation 2020) vs new infrastructure category (forward encoding models). TRIBE v2 (Meta FAIR) — predicts fMRI BOLD response across ~70,000 cortical voxels from video, trained on 1,000+ hours fMRI. MindEye/MindEye2 (Scotti et al., ICML 2024) — decode images from within-subject fMRI. Huth Lab semantic maps (Tang et al., Nature Neuroscience 2023). ORAM + TEE architecture for private long-term memory. Three contributions: KG-filtered search (metadata-only graph inside enclave, 13 pp accuracy gain matching Graphiti), oblivious dreaming (maintenance piggybacked on ordinary ORAM accesses), synthetic personal-data pipeline (Hawkes process, 6 modalities). Results: 29× throughput, 15× lower cost at 1M users ($1.40M vs $21.13M), 2.32s query latency. Under consideration for deployment to millions of users at a major AI provider.

The RSI model: free AI infrastructure, platform takes percentage of application revenues. Three generations of GenAI business models. Formal mathematical model (Stackelberg equilibrium, optimal commission α* = (1+c)/2). Comparative analysis across six models. DOI: 10.1007/s41412-026-00154-7. University of Cagliari. BOTTOM framework (Brain, Orientation, Transparency, Triggers, Objective, Mind). Integrates six validated taxonomies, extends MINDSPACE by decomposing each of nine categories into six analytical dimensions. Shifts from typology to mechanism. Application examples: vegetable consumption, vaccine adherence, dark nudges in finance.
859. **CONTEXT:** Poldrack (Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2006; Neuron, 2011) — The reverse-inference problem. Cannot infer cognitive process from regional activation without knowing region selectivity. Forward prediction routes around the problem; reverse inference does not. Foundational for the forward-prediction neuromarketing skill.
860. **CONTEXT:** Venkatraman et al. (JMR, 2015) — Ventral striatum fMRI signal uniquely predicted sales across 30 TV ads, incremental R² 0.10-0.14. Strongest single piece of evidence for neural data in advertising research.
861. **CONTEXT:** Mertens et al. (PNAS, 2021) — Meta-analysis of 447 choice architecture effect sizes, n=2,148,439, Cohen's d=0.43. Decision structure > decision information > decision assistance. Food choices 2.5× more responsive than financial. ~15% backfire. Foundational for the BOTTOM skill's mechanism explanation.
862. **CONTEXT:** Gandhi, Kiyawat, Tipton, Watts (2026) — "A meta-analytic database of 789 choice architecture interventions from 280 experiments coded on 298 variables." Open resource enabling mechanism-based meta-analysis.
863. **CONTEXT:** Keinan (Technion, 2025) — Game-theoretic model of revenue-sharing equilibria. "Full-sharing equilibrium profiles" where all creators voluntarily share content. Foundational for the RSI skill.
864. **CONTEXT:** Heimburg, Schreieck, Wiesche (JMIS, 2025) — Complementor value co-creation in GenAI platform ecosystems. Four co-creation mechanisms (system instructions, contextual data, user input curation, output revision). Foundational for the RSI skill.
